method: Official statute text read for each state (quotes machine-checked verbatim, 40 words max). true = the statute imposes the requirement or protection; null = silent; false = the statute expressly provides otherwise. The two classification fields are editorial judgments made from the recorded limits and penalties text. Revised 2026-09-27 after an independent review: frequency caps count only numeric limits; response periods count only time to respond, cure or resubmit to the manufacturer (not windows to sue or protest to a board); rate validation is "limited" only when the manufacturer has no right to request additional ROs or re-verify periodically and no comparison with other dealers.

audit_frequency_limit.limit: No more than one warranty audit of paid claims per calendar year. Incentive audits are separately limited to one per calendar year.
audit_frequency_limit.quote: The manufacturer may not perform more than one audit in a calendar year to determine the validity of paid claims for new motor vehicle dealer warranty work.
audit_frequency_limit.score_level_reason: At most one warranty audit of paid claims per calendar year.

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: Silent for chargebacks. Disapproval of a submitted claim requires written or electronic notice stating the reasons, but that governs initial claim review.

dealer_response_period.detail: No response period before a chargeback. A disapproved claim may be corrected and resubmitted within 30 days, but only as part of initial claim review.

internal_appeal.detail: The statute is silent.

chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.detail: The statute is silent.

clerical_error_protection.detail: The statute is silent.

documentation_limits.detail: Silent on audit documentation. § 45.25.200(a) only bars denying a claim for a condition found and properly repaired during a separate repair when the dealer provides the required documentation of need.

fraud_exception.detail: If the manufacturer reasonably suspects fraud, it may audit for fraudulent claims during any period in which a fraud action may be commenced. This applies to both the warranty and incentive limits.
fraud_exception.quote: if a manufacturer reasonably suspects fraud, the manufacturer may audit a dealer for fraudulent claims during any period in which an action for fraud may be commenced under applicable state law.

rate_submission_audit.limits: The manufacturer may disapprove within 30 days only by demonstrating that the rate is materially miscalculated or unreasonable compared with similarly situated Alaska dealers. For parts markup, it may not require any method other than the (d) RO method, or information that is unduly burdensome, including part-by-part or transaction-by-transaction calculations. There is no provision for requesting additional ROs or re-validating an existing rate.
rate_submission_audit.quote: may disapprove a rate proposed by the new motor vehicle dealer under this section if the manufacturer demonstrates that the proposed rate is materially miscalculated or unreasonable compared to other similarly situated new motor vehicle dealers

states.notes: The limits are framed as limits on initiating or conducting audits: within 1 year after payment, and one per calendar year. The statute does not separately regulate chargebacks. Incentive audits (AS 45.25.200(f)) must start within 1 year after payment or program end, whichever is later, and are limited to one per calendar year. Former AS 45.25.320 (claim-audit time limits) appears only as a repealed heading. No audit-specific penalty. No 2025-2026 amendment was found (the 34th Legislature was not exhaustively searched).

classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: Silent for chargebacks. Only a submitted claim must be 'specifically disapproved in writing' within 30 days, which governs initial claim review, not post-payment chargebacks.

dealer_response_period.detail: No response or rebuttal period before a chargeback. (A dealer may file an amended claim within 120 days after neglect, oversight or mistake, but that is a claim-filing rule.)

internal_appeal.detail: The statute is silent.

chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.detail: The statute is silent.

clerical_error_protection.detail: A warrantor may not unreasonably disapprove a claim solely because of an incidental failure to meet a claim-processing requirement that results only in a clerical or administrative error. The text addresses disapproval, not chargebacks expressly, but chargebacks are allowed only for fraudulent claims anyway. The same rule applies to incentive claims (§ 8-20-4(3)u.).
clerical_error_protection.quote: nor shall the warrantor unreasonably disapprove a claim solely based on the dealer’s incidental failure to comply with a specific claim processing requirement that results only in a clerical error or administrative error

documentation_limits.detail: A denial must rest on a material defect and deviation from the manufacturer's REASONABLE WRITTEN claim-submission requirements. Preauthorized claims may not be disapproved. Same for incentive claims.
documentation_limits.quote: a claim denial must be based upon a material defect and deviation from the reasonable written claim submission requirements of the manufacturer

fraud_exception.detail: No fraud carve-out. The audit and chargeback right is itself limited to FRAUDULENT claims, and even those are capped at 12 months from payment (same for incentives under § 8-20-4(3)u.).
fraud_exception.quote: the warrantor retains the right to audit such claims and to charge back the dealer for any fraudulent claims for a period not to exceed 12 months from the date the claim was paid

rate_submission_audit.limits: Within 45 days the warrantor may rebut once by reasonably substantiating that the submission is materially incomplete, inaccurate or unreasonable, with a full explanation, evidence for each reason, all calculations and a proposed adjusted rate. It may not later expand the rebuttal except for information it did not have. If the calculated rate is substantially higher or lower than the rate on record, it may request additional ROs for 60 days before or after the submitted period, then has 45 days from receipt to rebut. Submissions are limited to once per 12 months.
rate_submission_audit.quote: the warrantor, in accordance with this subsection, may request additional repair orders for a period of 60 days prior to or 60 days subsequent to the time period for which the repair orders were submitted

states.notes: Text read from ALISON (official) via its code API. Audits and chargebacks are limited to FRAUDULENT claims within 12 months of payment. Warranty (§ 8-20-7(e)) and incentive (§ 8-20-4(3)u.) rules are parallel. § 8-20-7.1(e)-(f) (recall/stop-sale claims) cross-references the audit provisions of 'subsection (d)' of § 8-20-7, but they are actually in (e). No audit-specific penalty. General remedies are elsewhere in ch. 20 (§§ 8-20-11, -12) and were not re-read. Last amended by Act 2022-104. No 2023-2026 amendment was found.

classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: Silent for chargebacks. Disapproval of a submitted claim requires written notice stating specific grounds ((e)(2)(A)(i)). The chargeback appeal clock runs from 'notification' by the manufacturer, but no written-grounds requirement is stated for chargebacks.

dealer_response_period.detail: No rebuttal period before a chargeback. The dealer has 90 days from notification to appeal a chargeback to the Arkansas Motor Vehicle Commission (see chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal).

internal_appeal.detail: Not required. (e)(3)(B) says a dealer 'may contest the disapproval through the manufacturer's appeals process' (clerical-error disapprovals), but it does not require the manufacturer to maintain one. Nothing addresses chargebacks.
internal_appeal.quote: However, a dealer may contest the disapproval through the manufacturer's appeals process.

chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.detail: The dealer may appeal any (e)(4) chargeback to the Arkansas Motor Vehicle Commission within 90 days of notification. Once an appeal is filed, the chargeback may not be levied until the appeal is resolved. The hearing must be held within 120 days unless the parties settle. This covers warranty and, through (e)(4)(B), incentive and reimbursement programs.
chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.quote: If a dealer files an appeal of the chargeback with the commission, the manufacturer or distributor shall not levy the chargeback until the appeal is resolved.

clerical_error_protection.detail: A claim may not be disapproved for a clerical error that does not make the claim amount incorrect, including errors caused by the manufacturer's prior-approval process. Act 1055 of 2015 struck the former preapproval proviso. The text addresses disapproval; chargebacks are limited to 'false or unsubstantiated claims'.
clerical_error_protection.quote: A claim shall not be disapproved because a clerical error was made that does not render the amount of the claim incorrect

documentation_limits.detail: No limit stated. (e)(4)(A)(i) expressly lets the manufacturer 'Require documentation for claims'.

fraud_exception.detail: A fraudulent claim may be charged back up to 2 years from the claim date, but only if the manufacturer establishes the fraud in an Arkansas court of competent jurisdiction.
fraud_exception.quote: the manufacturer retains the right to charge back any fraudulent claim if the manufacturer establishes in a court of competent jurisdiction in this state that the claim is fraudulent

rate_submission_audit.limits: The manufacturer must approve or disapprove a rate-change request within 45 days, or it is deemed approved. If the calculated rate is substantially higher or lower than the rate on record, it may request additional documentation for 45 days before or after the submitted period. The rate must be reasonable compared with same line-make dealers in an economically similar area or the dealer's competitive market area (§ 23-112-313(c)(3)). There is no frequency limit.
rate_submission_audit.quote: may request additional documentation for a period of either forty-five (45) days prior or forty-five (45) days subsequent to the time period for which the repair orders were submitted
rate_submission_audit.pinpoint: Ark. Code Ann. § 23-112-310(d)(1)(D)(iii) (added by Act 1077 of 2021, § 4); see (d)(1)(D)(i)-(ii)

penalties_for_audit_violations.detail: Chargeback appeal to the Arkansas Motor Vehicle Commission, with an automatic bar on levying the chargeback while the appeal is pending. There is no audit-specific monetary penalty.
penalties_for_audit_violations.quote: A dealer may file an appeal with the Arkansas Motor Vehicle Commission to protest any chargeback under this subdivision (e)(4) within ninety (90) days of notification by the manufacturer or distributor.
penalties_for_audit_violations.pinpoint: Ark. Code Ann. § 23-112-313(e)(4)(D)(i), (iii) (appeal under § 23-112-501 et seq.)

states.notes: Audit and chargeback rules: audits within 1 year from payment or credit; chargebacks only for 'false or unsubstantiated claims'; the manufacturer may require documentation. The same rules apply to all other incentive and reimbursement programs for 12 months after the transaction date ((e)(4)(B)). The official consolidated code is Lexis-hosted and was not read. The current (e) text comes from the 2011 Official Edition PDF (AMVC, labor.arkansas.gov), enrolled Act 756/2009 § 12 (which wrote (e)(4)), and Act 1055/2015 § 5. Strike-through was read from the PDF: it removed the preapproval proviso from (e)(3)(A). The Justia 2024 mirror confirms the result. Later acts (924/2019, 1077/2021, 515/2023) did not touch (e). The 2025 session was not exhaustively checked.

classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.

audit_frequency_limit.quote: may reasonably and periodically audit a new motor vehicle dealer to determine the validity of paid claims for dealer compensation or any charge-backs for warranty parts or service compensation
audit_frequency_limit.detail: Qualitative only (e.g., "reasonable" or "periodic" audits); no numeric cap. Qualitative only: audits must be 'reasonable and periodic'. There is no numeric cap.

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: A chargeback may follow only after the dealer has had 'notice' and a chance to use any available mediation. The statute does not say the notice must be written or state grounds.
written_reasons_before_chargeback.quote: the right to charge back to the new motor vehicle dealer the amount of any previously paid claim after the new motor vehicle dealer has had notice and an opportunity to participate in any available manufacturer or distributor mediation processes

dealer_response_period.detail: No fixed number of days.

internal_appeal.detail: A chargeback must wait until the dealer has had the chance to use 'any available' manufacturer or distributor mediation. The statute does not require the manufacturer to offer mediation.
internal_appeal.quote: the right to charge back to the new motor vehicle dealer the amount of any previously paid claim after the new motor vehicle dealer has had notice and an opportunity to participate in any available manufacturer or distributor mediation processes

chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.detail: No chargeback until the dealer has had notice and a chance to use any available mediation. If mediation fails, no chargeback until all legal appeals are exhausted. The same applies to incentive audits (H).
chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.quote: and all legal appeals have been exhausted if mediation failed to result in an agreement

clerical_error_protection.detail: A properly submitted warranty or incentive claim may not be denied based solely on an incidental failure to meet a claim-processing requirement that does not question the claim's legitimacy. The dealer may correct and resubmit within 60 days of first notice. The text addresses denial, not post-audit chargebacks expressly.
clerical_error_protection.quote: based solely on a new motor vehicle dealer's incidental failure to comply with a specific claim processing requirement that does not put into question the legitimacy of the claim

documentation_limits.detail: The statute is silent.

fraud_exception.detail: The 12-month audit window does not apply if the manufacturer reasonably suspects fraud. The same applies to incentive audits (H).
fraud_exception.quote: This limitation does not apply if the manufacturer, factory branch, distributor or distributor branch reasonably suspects fraud.

rate_submission_audit.limits: Within 30 days the manufacturer may rebut the presumption by reasonably substantiating that the rates are inaccurate or unreasonable compared with similarly situated same line-make Arizona dealers, and it must propose an adjustment (E). It may use the submitted ROs to validate any or all current warranty rates, or require the dealer to submit ROs to validate its retail rates not more than once every 12 months. If a retail rate has declined, it may reduce the warranty rate prospectively (K). It may not require an unduly burdensome method, including part-by-part or transaction-by-transaction calculations (K).
rate_submission_audit.quote: may use the repair orders submitted by a new motor vehicle dealer under subsection E of this section to validate any or all of a new motor vehicle dealer's current warranty reimbursement rates

more_quotes.quote: require a new motor vehicle dealer to submit, not more than once every twelve months, repair orders pursuant to this section to validate the new motor vehicle dealer's retail rate or rates

states.notes: Warranty (G) and incentive (H) audit rules are parallel. Each allows a 12-month or one-year window from payment. A reasonable suspicion of fraud lifts the window. A chargeback may follow only after notice, a chance to use any available mediation and, if mediation fails, exhaustion of legal appeals. No audit-specific penalty. Last amended by Laws 2024, ch. 94 (per prior research). No 2025-2026 amendment was found.

classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.

advance_notice.detail: Only for an additional (non-random) audit within the 9-month period: the notification to the dealer must be accompanied by written disclosure of the basis for the audit.
advance_notice.quote: The franchisor’s notification to the franchisee of any additional audit within a nine-month period shall be accompanied by written disclosure of the basis for that additional audit.

selection_basis_disclosed.detail: Required only for an ADDITIONAL audit within a 9-month period, beyond the one allowed random audit. The notice must be accompanied by written disclosure of the basis for that audit. Selection may never be punitive, retaliatory or unfairly discriminatory. The same rule applies to incentive audits (§ 3065.1(g)(1)).
selection_basis_disclosed.quote: The franchisor’s notification to the franchisee of any additional audit within a nine-month period shall be accompanied by written disclosure of the basis for that additional audit.

audit_frequency_limit.limit: No more than one random audit per 9-month period. Additional audits in that period require written disclosure of their basis. Audits must be on a reasonable basis, within 9 months after payment or credit.
audit_frequency_limit.quote: A franchisor may conduct no more than one random audit of a franchisee in a nine-month period.
audit_frequency_limit.score_level_reason: One random audit per 9-month period; more are allowed with written disclosure of their basis.

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: Within 30 days after the audit, the franchisor must give a written disapproval notice stating the specific grounds. If the franchisee appeals and the franchisor still denies, it must send a written 'Final Denial' notice within 30 days after the appeal ends.
written_reasons_before_chargeback.quote: the franchisor shall provide to the franchisee, within 30 days after the audit, a written disapproval notice stating the specific grounds upon which the claim is disapproved.

dealer_response_period.detail: At least 30 days after receiving the written disapproval notice to rebut and cure, scaled to the volume of claims. No chargeback until 45 days after the later written notice (disapproval or Final Denial). The chargeback must be taken within 90 days of that notice.
dealer_response_period.quote: a reasonable period of not less than 30 days after receipt of the written disapproval notice to respond to any disapproval

internal_appeal.detail: The franchisor must provide a reasonable appeal process. If the franchisee rebuts and cures before the deadline, there is no chargeback for that claim.
internal_appeal.quote: The franchisor shall provide a reasonable appeal process allowing the franchisee a reasonable period of not less than 30 days after receipt of the written disapproval notice

chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.detail: If a New Motor Vehicle Board protest (due within 6 months) is filed before the chargeback, the franchisor may not offset or collect until the Board issues a final order. After the order, it has 90 days to charge back. This is on top of the 45-day hold after the written notice.
chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.quote: the franchisor shall not offset or otherwise undertake to collect the chargeback until the board issues a final order on the protest.

extrapolation.detail: Extrapolation from a sample is allowed only if the sample is selected randomly and the extrapolation is reasonable and statistically valid. The same rule applies to incentives (§ 3065.1(g)(2)).
extrapolation.quote: A franchisor shall not disapprove or chargeback a claim based upon an extrapolation from a sample of claims, unless the sample of claims is selected randomly and the extrapolation is performed in a reasonable and statistically valid manner.

clerical_error_protection.detail: Documentation or administrative noncompliance supports a chargeback only if MATERIAL, and the franchisee has at least 30 days to cure it. A cured claim may not be charged back.
clerical_error_protection.quote: If the franchisee rebuts any disapproval and cures any material noncompliance relating to a claim before the applicable deadline, the franchisor shall not chargeback the franchisee for that claim.

documentation_limits.detail: Documentation grounds are limited to MATERIAL noncompliance with REASONABLE and NONDISCRIMINATORY documentation and administrative claim-submission requirements. Incentive claims may also be charged back if 'ineligible under the terms of the incentive program as previously communicated to the franchisee' (§ 3065.1(g)(2)).
documentation_limits.quote: or for material noncompliance with reasonable and nondiscriminatory documentation and administrative claims submission requirements

fraud_exception.detail: A longer audit and chargeback period for a false claim submitted with intent to defraud is allowed only if the franchisor obtains an order from the New Motor Vehicle Board.
fraud_exception.quote: If a false claim was submitted by a franchisee with the intent to defraud the franchisor, a longer period for audit and any resulting chargeback may be permitted if the franchisor obtains an order from the board.

rate_submission_audit.limits: The franchisor may contest material accuracy within 30 days with ONE notification, limited to an assertion that the rate is materially inaccurate or fraudulent. The notification must give a full explanation, evidence, all calculations and a proposed adjusted rate. The franchisor may not deny the submission. If the submitted rate is substantially higher than the current warranty rate, it may request in writing, within 30 days, all ROs closed in the 30 days immediately before or after the submitted set, and may then recalculate using the statutory method and exclusions. It may not substitute another sample, unilaterally calculate a rate, use part-by-part or transaction-by-transaction calculations or financial statements, or use a parts sample to cut the labor rate (or the reverse). It may not conduct or threaten nonroutine or nonrandom audits in response to a rate request.
rate_submission_audit.quote: may request, in writing, within 30 days after the franchisor’s receipt of the notice submitted pursuant to subdivision (a), all repair orders closed within the period of 30 days immediately preceding, or 30 days immediately following

more_quotes.quote: Conducting or threatening to conduct nonroutine or nonrandom warranty, nonwarranty repair, or other service-related audits in response to a franchisee seeking compensation or exercising any right pursuant to this section.

penalties_for_audit_violations.detail: The franchisee may protest to the New Motor Vehicle Board within 6 months after the written disapproval notice or the end of the appeal process. The franchisor bears the burden of proof, and collection is stayed while the protest is pending. Rate disputes go to the Board under § 3065.4 (franchisor burden, Board may determine the underpayment, superior-court enforcement).
penalties_for_audit_violations.quote: In any protest pursuant to this subdivision, the franchisor shall have the burden of proof.

states.notes: Warranty (§ 3065(e)-(f)) and incentive (§ 3065.1(g)-(h)) audit procedures are parallel: 9-month lookback from payment or credit, one random audit per 9 months, the random/statistically-valid extrapolation rule, written grounds within 30 days, at least 30 days to rebut or cure, a 45-day chargeback hold, a 90-day chargeback deadline and a Board-protest stay. They differ on chargeback grounds: incentives may be charged back as 'ineligible under the terms of the incentive program as previously communicated'. Credit lines: § 3065 Stats. 2019 ch. 796 (AB 179), eff. 1/1/2020; § 3065.1 Stats. 2013 ch. 512 (SB 155); § 3065.2 Stats. 2020 ch. 370; § 3065.4 added Stats. 2019 ch. 796. No 2025-2026 amendment was found. 2026 bills awaiting signature (effective 1/1/2027) were not exhaustively checked.

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: The statute is silent.

dealer_response_period.detail: No rebuttal period. The dealer has 30 days to ask the executive director to rule that a chargeback violates the time limits (see chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal).

internal_appeal.detail: The statute is silent.

chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.detail: The stay applies only to a dealer's timely request (within 30 days) for an executive-director determination that the chargeback violates the § 44-20-135(1) time limits. It is not a general merits appeal.
chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.quote: If a determination is requested within the thirty-day period, then the charge back, reimbursement, or credit shall be stayed pending the decision of the executive director.

clerical_error_protection.detail: The statute is silent.

documentation_limits.detail: A timing limit only. No documentation demand or audit more than 15 months after claim submission. No chargeback, reimbursement or credit arising from an audit or documentation request made more than 9 months after submission. The statute sets no substantive documentation standard.
documentation_limits.quote: shall not require documentation for warranty, sales, or incentive claims or audit warranty, sales, or incentive claims of a motor vehicle dealer more than fifteen months after the date the claim was submitted

fraud_exception.detail: The audit limits do not restrict a fraud action brought in court. The statute provides no longer administrative audit window.
fraud_exception.quote: Subsection (1) of this section shall not limit any action for fraud instituted in a court of competent jurisdiction.

rate_submission_audit.limits: The manufacturer may conduct a periodic review of service records to verify the continuing accuracy of the proposed or in-effect rate, not more than once per calendar year. This review is not an 'audit' under § 44-20-135. If the submitted rates are 10% higher or lower than current rates, it may request additional ROs for the 90 days before or after the submitted ROs. It may contest within 45 days with an explanation, evidence and a proposed adjustment, and may modify its reasons only on discovery of new relevant information. It may not require unduly burdensome information, including part-by-part or transaction-by-transaction calculations.
rate_submission_audit.quote: A manufacturer shall not conduct a periodic review more than once per calendar year. This periodic review is not an audit in accordance with section 44-20-135.

more_quotes.quote: If the rates from the calculation are ten percent higher or lower than the current rates, the manufacturer may request additional repair orders for the ninety days before or after the submitted repair orders for purposes of alteration.

penalties_for_audit_violations.detail: A chargeback, reimbursement or credit that the executive director finds (after a hearing) violates the § 44-20-135(1) time limits is void.
penalties_for_audit_violations.quote: If the executive director determines after a hearing that the charge back, reimbursement, or credit violates subsection (1) of this section, the charge back, reimbursement, or credit shall be void.

states.notes: One rule set covers warranty, sales and incentive claims. The 9-month audit and chargeback window runs from claim SUBMISSION, not payment. No 2025-2026 amendment was found; SB 25-160 amended other part 1 sections. Watch item: part 1 of article 20 is set to repeal September 1, 2027, subject to sunset review (§ 44-20-142).

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: The statute is silent.

dealer_response_period.detail: After a denial or chargeback for a processing, clerical or administrative failure, the dealer may resubmit the claim within 30 days under reasonable manufacturer or distributor guidelines. Fraud excepted.
dealer_response_period.quote: shall allow the dealer to resubmit such claim according to reasonable manufacturer or distributor guidelines not later than thirty days after the initial claim denial or charge-back

internal_appeal.detail: The statute is silent.

chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.detail: The statute is silent.

clerical_error_protection.detail: No denial, and no post-audit charge-back, based solely on a failure to follow a claim-processing procedure, a clerical error or another administrative technicality that does not call the claim's legitimacy into question. This covers warranty and sales-incentive, marketing and advertising claims.
clerical_error_protection.quote: A manufacturer or distributor shall not deny a claim submitted under this subsection or charge-back such a claim or payment following a timely audit based solely on the dealer's failure to comply with a claim processing procedure

documentation_limits.detail: Not counted: § 42-133s(j) sets no documentation standard for audits or chargebacks. Limited. The only express limit is that dealers need keep defective parts no longer than 90 days after claim submission. The statute sets no documentation standard; charge-backs are allowed for "false or unsubstantiated claims".
documentation_limits.quote: Dealers shall be required to maintain defective parts for a period of not longer than ninety days following submission of claims.

fraud_exception.detail: With evidence of fraud, the one-year limit does not restrict longer audits or charge-back of fraudulent claims.
fraud_exception.quote: If there is evidence of fraud, the provisions of this subsection shall not limit the right of a manufacturer or distributor to audit a dealer for longer periods of time and charge-back the dealer for any fraudulent claim.

rate_submission_audit.limits: Declared parts markup (b) and labor rate (c) take effect 30 days after declaration, 'subject to audit of the submitted repair orders by the franchisor' and rebuttal. A rebuttal is due within 30 days, reasonably substantiating that the rate is unfair and unreasonable in light of all other same line-make franchised dealers in the vicinity, and must propose an adjustment. rate_submission_audit.quote: The average labor rate shall go into effect thirty days following the declaration, subject to audit of the submitted repair orders by the franchisor and a rebuttal of such declared rate.
rate_submission_audit.pinpoint: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 42-133s(c); see (b) (parts, same audit language), (f)

states.notes: Subsection (j) applies one rule to warranty labor and parts claims and to sales incentive, marketing and advertising program claims. Audits and charge-backs are allowed only for false or unsubstantiated claims within one year following payment. P.A. 15-191 cut the period from 2 years to 1 and added the clerical-error protection. The audit text is otherwise unchanged. No audit-specific penalty; general remedies elsewhere in ch. 739 (e.g., § 42-133ee) are not audit-specific.

classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: No written-grounds notice is required for each chargeback. A chargeback for failure to follow claim-documentation procedures requires a prior certified-mail written warning (see documentation_limits).

dealer_response_period.detail: The statute is silent.

internal_appeal.detail: The statute is silent.

chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.detail: The statute is silent.

clerical_error_protection.detail: No denial or chargeback because of a dealer administrative error, if the claim can be substantiated under the manufacturer's reasonable policies or by other reasonable means.
clerical_error_protection.quote: A claim may not be denied or charged back due to an administrative error by the dealer as long as the claim meets the above requirements.

documentation_limits.detail: (d)(1): no denial or reduction if the dealer gives reasonably sufficient documentation that it made a good-faith attempt to follow the manufacturer's reasonable written policies and actually did the work. (d)(2): the dealer may substantiate a claim under the manufacturer's reasonable policies 'or by other reasonable means'. (d)(3): no chargeback for failing claim-documentation procedures unless the same specific failure happened within the prior 12 months AND the manufacturer sent a certified-mail written warning naming the procedure within the prior 12 months. For incentives, substantiation may be by reasonable written procedures or other reasonable means ((f)).
documentation_limits.quote: The manufacturer or distributor may not disapprove or charge back a reimbursement claim provided that the dealer can substantiate the claim either in accordance with the manufacturer’s reasonable policies and procedures or by other reasonable means.

more_quotes.quote: The manufacturer has, within the previous 12 months, provided a written warning to the dealer by certified United States mail, return receipt requested, identifying the specific claim documentation procedure violated by the dealer.

fraud_exception.detail: The 180-day warranty audit limit and the 180-day post-program incentive audit limit do not apply to fraudulent claims.
fraud_exception.quote: The 180-day limitation on the manufacturer’s right to audit a claim shall not be effect in the case of fraudulent claims.

more_quotes.quote: These limitations shall not be in effect in the case of fraudulent claims.

rate_submission_audit.limits: Within 30 days after receiving the declared schedule, the manufacturer may make reasonable requests for additional supporting information. The 30-day effective-date clock then runs from receipt of that information. It may not require any other methodology or unduly burdensome supporting information, including part-by-part or transaction-by-transaction calculations. The dealer may request a change at most once every 9 months. A denial may be protested to the Public Service Commission within 30 days, and the manufacturer bears the burden.
rate_submission_audit.quote: within 30 days following receipt of the declared schedule of compensation from the dealer, the manufacturer may make reasonable requests for additional information supporting the declared schedule of compensation.

states.notes: Warranty window: 180 days following payment. 84 Del. Laws c. 389 (2024) cut it from 1 year. Warranty chargebacks are allowed only for fraud, work done unnecessarily, or work not properly performed ((d)(1)). Incentive audits may cover only the 180 days following termination of the incentive program ((e)). Incentive denials, reductions or chargebacks require a false or fraudulent claim or a failure to reasonably substantiate it ((f)). § 4903(d)(2) literally reads 'shall not be effect' (drafting glitch). No audit-specific penalty; general civil remedies are in § 4916. No 2025-2026 amendment appears on delcode.

classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.

advance_notice.detail: There is no pre-audit notice requirement.

selection_basis_disclosed.detail: Verified. At the required post-audit meeting (within 30 days after a timely audit, before any chargeback), the licensee must give a WRITTEN statement of the basis on which the dealer was selected for audit or review. This applies to warranty, maintenance, service and incentive audits.
selection_basis_disclosed.quote: a written statement containing the basis upon which the motor vehicle dealer was selected for audit or review.

audit_frequency_limit.limit: No warranty, retail customer repair or other service-related audit more than once each calendar year. Conducting or threatening one is prohibited 'adverse action' against a dealer seeking compensation under § 320.696. Audits must also be 'reasonable and periodic' (§ 320.64(25)). The calendar-year cap does not expressly mention incentive audits.
audit_frequency_limit.quote: conducting or threatening to conduct any warranty, retail customer repair, or other service-related audit more frequently than once each calendar year
audit_frequency_limit.score_level_reason: At most one warranty or service audit per calendar year.

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: Within 30 days after a timely audit, a licensee representative must meet the dealer's designee (in person, by phone or by video). It must give a detailed explanation, with supporting documentation, of the basis for each proposed chargeback, plus the written selection-basis statement. After internal dispute processes, it must give written notice of the final proposed chargeback amount. The basis may not change later unless new information arrives within 30 days after the audit.
written_reasons_before_chargeback.quote: the applicant or licensee must provide a detailed explanation, with supporting documentation, as to the basis for each of the claims for which the applicant or licensee proposed a chargeback to the dealer

dealer_response_period.detail: A reasonable period after the meeting, scaled to claim volume, but never less than 45 days. The dealer gets the same meeting and response rights if the licensee claims new information.
dealer_response_period.quote: in no case less than 45 days after the meeting.

internal_appeal.detail: Not mandated. The statute has the final chargeback notice come after 'all internal dispute resolution processes provided through the applicant or licensee' are completed, but it does not require the licensee to offer one.
internal_appeal.quote: After all internal dispute resolution processes provided through the applicant or licensee have been completed, the applicant or licensee shall give written notice to the motor vehicle dealer of the final amount of its proposed chargeback.

chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.detail: The dealer may protest to the Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles within 30 days of the final notice. The licensee may not act to recover until the department makes a final, unappealable determination. The licensee bears the burden of proof.
chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.quote: the applicant or licensee may not take any action to recover the amount of the proposed chargeback until the department renders a final determination

extrapolation.detail: Not addressed expressly. § 320.64(25) lets the licensee charge back only the portion of a claim it has shown to be improper, which implies claim-by-claim proof, but the statute says nothing about extrapolation. There is no express extrapolation clause. The limit is implied: a chargeback is allowed 'only' for the portion of a claim the licensee has PROVEN false, fraudulent or noncompliant, with a documented basis for each claim. This effectively requires claim-by-claim proof.
extrapolation.quote: an applicant or licensee may deny or charge back only that portion of a warranty, maintenance, or other service-related claim or incentive claim which the applicant or licensee has proven to be false or fraudulent

clerical_error_protection.detail: Denying, reducing or charging back a warranty claim because the dealer failed to meet ALL of the licensee's claim description or processing requirements is prohibited 'adverse action' (§ 320.696(2)). Chargebacks require a failure to SUBSTANTIALLY comply (§ 320.64(25)).
clerical_error_protection.quote: denying, reducing, or charging back a warranty claim because of a dealer’s failure to comply with all of the licensee’s requirements for describing or processing a claim.

documentation_limits.detail: Procedural chargebacks are allowed only for failure to substantially comply with the licensee's REASONABLE, WRITTEN and UNIFORMLY APPLIED procedures, and only for the portion shown. The licensee may not impose claim terms, policies or procedures different from § 320.696 (§ 320.696(1)(c)).
documentation_limits.quote: the motor vehicle dealer failed to substantially comply with the reasonable written and uniformly applied procedures of the applicant or licensee for such repairs or incentives

fraud_exception.detail: There is no fraud carve-out from the 12-month window. After 12 months, warranty and incentive payments are final 'for any reason notwithstanding any otherwise applicable law'. Within the window, fraud is a chargeback ground.
fraud_exception.quote: all warranty, maintenance, and other service-related payments and incentive payments shall be deemed final and incontrovertible for any reason notwithstanding any otherwise applicable law

rate_submission_audit.limits: Limited. For a parts-markup request, the dealer must give 10 days' written notice, and within that period the licensee may pick the first of the 50 consecutive retail ROs used (§ 320.696(3)(a)1.). The licensee may not 'review, change, or fail to pay' parts or labor compensation unless the dealer requested a change or under its written, predetermined increase schedule (§ 320.696(5)). No retail-customer-repair audit more than once per calendar year (§ 320.696(2)). The dealer must attach supporting documentation, and requests are limited to twice a year. The statute has no rebuttal or contest procedure.
rate_submission_audit.quote: A licensee shall not review, change, or fail to pay a motor vehicle dealer for parts or labor determined under this section unless the dealer has requested a change

more_quotes.quote: permit the licensee, within that 10-day period, to select the initial retail customer repair for the consecutive repair orders that will be attached to the written request used for the markup computation

penalties_for_audit_violations.detail: An audit conducted in violation of § 320.64, or any failure to comply with § 320.696, is itself a listed ground in § 320.64(25). With proof of a pattern, the license may be denied, suspended or revoked. The licensee is also liable under § 320.695 (injunction) and § 320.697 (treble damages, costs and attorney's fees; the burden shifts to the licensee on a prima facie showing). A DHSMV protest stays collection, with the burden on the licensee.
penalties_for_audit_violations.quote: The applicant or licensee has undertaken or engaged in an audit of warranty, maintenance, and other service-related payments or incentive payments

more_quotes.quote: has a cause of action against the licensee for damages and may recover damages therefor in any court of competent jurisdiction in an amount equal to 3 times the pecuniary loss

states.notes: Selection-basis disclosure is confirmed: a written statement is required at the post-audit meeting. § 320.64(25) applies one procedure to warranty, maintenance and service audits and to incentive audits (each 12 months from payment). The once-per-calendar-year cap is in the § 320.696(2) definition of 'adverse action' and names warranty, retail customer repair and service audits, not incentive audits. Text read from the 2026 Florida Statutes. The § 320.64 history runs through ch. 2026-39. Ch. 2025-38 added § 320.64(43), a general anti-retaliation ground (not audit-specific). Ch. 2026-39 amends other § 320.64 subsections effective 10/1/2026 (not audit-related).

classification.rate_validation_basis: Limited: the manufacturer may check the rate only against the dealer's own submitted ROs (or has no rebuttal right at all), with no right to request additional ROs or run periodic re-verification, and no comparison with other dealers' rates.
classification.audit_consequence_basis: An audit conducted in violation of § 320.64, or any failure to comply with § 320.696, is itself a listed ground in § 320.64(25). With proof of a pattern, the license may be denied, suspended or revoked. The licensee is also liable under § 320.695 (injunction) and § 320.697 (treble damages, costs and attorney's fees; the burden shifts to the licensee on a prima facie showing). A DHSMV protest stays collection, with the burden on the licensee.

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: The franchisor must 'send a notice to such dealer for such amount' it claims from an audit. The statute does not say the notice must be written or state grounds, though at any hearing the franchisor must prove the grounds.
written_reasons_before_chargeback.quote: such franchisor shall send a notice to such dealer for such amount and the dealer shall have not less than 30 days to contest such amount or remit payment.

dealer_response_period.detail: At least 30 days after the notice to contest the amount or pay. If the dealer contests, the charge is stayed.
dealer_response_period.quote: such franchisor shall send a notice to such dealer for such amount and the dealer shall have not less than 30 days to contest such amount or remit payment.

internal_appeal.detail: Conditional. Once the dealer contests, the parties 'shall attempt' internal dispute resolution through the franchisor's procedure 'if available', within a reasonable time. The statute does not require a procedure to exist.
internal_appeal.quote: the parties shall attempt to resolve the dispute through an internal dispute resolution procedure of the franchisor, if available, provided that such procedure occurs within a reasonable amount of time.

chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.detail: The charge is stayed through internal dispute resolution and any petition to the commissioner. The petition is due by the later of 60 days after the notice or 30 days after internal dispute resolution ends. The franchisor bears the burden by a preponderance.
chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.quote: If the dealer contests such amount, the charge shall be stayed pending a final resolution as provided in this Code section.

extrapolation.detail: There is no sampling or extrapolation rule. § 10-1-662(a)(13) only bars applying audit results to transactions more than one year before the audit (a time limit).
extrapolation.quote: or to apply the results of an audit, investigation, or inquiry to any activity, transaction, conduct, or other occurrence which took place more than one year prior to such audit, investigation, or inquiry

clerical_error_protection.detail: No charge-back, deduction or reduction based solely on a clerical error that does not question the claim's legitimacy. A claim rejected for clerical error may be resubmitted in corrected form within 30 days.
clerical_error_protection.quote: shall not charge back to, deduct from, or reduce any account of a dealer or any amount owed to a dealer based solely on such dealer’s clerical error that does not put into question the legitimacy of the claim

documentation_limits.detail: A charge-back requires the franchisor to show by a preponderance that the transaction was fraudulent, intentionally and materially false, not reasonably substantiated, or did not follow the franchisor's WRITTEN repair or claim-submission requirements ((a)(14)). Denial, delay, restriction or bill-back of warranty, incentive, holdback or special-program claims is allowed only for a material defect affecting the claim's validity ((a)(15)).
documentation_limits.quote: unless such denial, delay, restriction, or bill back is the direct result of a material defect in the claim which affects the validity of the claim

fraud_exception.detail: If the franchisor has reason to believe fraudulent or intentionally false claims were submitted, it may extend the audit period, but never beyond 4 years before the audit. The (a)(14) charge-back limit (one year from transaction to notice) has no express fraud extension.
fraud_exception.quote: If the franchisor has reason to believe that fraudulent or intentionally false claims have been submitted, the franchisor may extend the audit, investigation, or inquiry period beyond the time periods provided in this paragraph

rate_submission_audit.limits: If the calculated parts or labor rate is substantially higher or lower than the rate on record, the franchisor may request additional documentation for 60 days before or after the submitted period. It must approve or disapprove within 30 days (deemed approved otherwise). It may contest within 30 days by reasonably substantiating that the rate is unreasonable against similarly situated same line-make dealers in a comparable Georgia area (a parts contest needs a written explanation), and must propose an adjustment. Internal dispute resolution applies if available (up to 30 days), then a petition to the commissioner with the franchisor bearing the burden. It may not require an unduly burdensome method. The dealer may declare at most once per calendar year.
rate_submission_audit.quote: may request additional documentation for a period of either 60 days prior to or 60 days subsequent to the time period for which the repair orders were submitted for purposes of an adjustment

penalties_for_audit_violations.detail: Petition to the commissioner and a hearing at which the franchisor must prove the chargeback grounds by a preponderance. The charge is stayed meanwhile. There is no audit-specific monetary penalty.
penalties_for_audit_violations.quote: In any hearing held pursuant to this paragraph, the burden of proof shall be upon the franchisor to demonstrate by a preponderance of evidence

states.notes: § 10-1-662(a)(13)-(15) apply to any audit, investigation or inquiry, and to warranty, incentive, holdback and special-program money alike. The (a)(14) one-year charge-back lookback runs from the transaction to the NOTICE of charge-back, not from payment. The (a)(13) audit lookback is one year before the audit. Text was read from the official O.C.G.A. as released by the Code Revision Commission via Public.Resource.Org/UniCourt (release 86, Nov. 2022); (a)(13)-(14) were last rewritten by SB 122 (2019). Legislative Counsel summaries show 2023, 2024 and 2026 acts did not amend § 10-1-662. SB 81 (2025) revised only (a)(1), (20) and (21) and added (22), none of them audit-related.

classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: Written notice is required 30 days before a proposed chargeback is imposed. The statute does not say the notice must state grounds.
written_reasons_before_chargeback.quote: The manufacturer or distributor shall provide the dealer a written notice thirty days before imposing a proposed chargeback.

dealer_response_period.detail: The written notice must come 30 days before imposition, and the dealer may protest before the chargeback is imposed.
dealer_response_period.quote: The dealer may protest the imposition of a proposed chargeback prior to the imposition of a proposed chargeback.

internal_appeal.detail: Conditional. The parties 'shall conduct any internal dispute resolution process in accordance with the franchise agreement', which applies only if the agreement provides one.
internal_appeal.quote: The dealer, manufacturer, or distributor shall conduct any internal dispute resolution process in accordance with the franchise agreement.

chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.detail: After internal dispute resolution, the dealer may petition the Department of Commerce and Consumer Affairs under § 437-51. The chargeback is then stayed for the entire action, until final judgment.
chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.quote: If a petition is filed, the proposed chargeback shall be stayed during the entirety of the action and until a final judgment has been rendered.

clerical_error_protection.detail: There is no express clerical-error rule. Chargebacks require a failure to SUBSTANTIALLY comply with reasonable written procedures (see documentation_limits).

documentation_limits.detail: A chargeback of sales or warranty payments requires the manufacturer to carry its burden of proving fraud, or that the dealer did not substantially comply with the manufacturer's REASONABLE WRITTEN procedures.
documentation_limits.quote: unless the manufacturer or distributor can satisfy its burden of proof that the dealer's claim was fraudulent or that the dealer did not substantially comply with the reasonable written procedures of the manufacturer or distributor.

fraud_exception.detail: The one-year audit and chargeback limit does not apply to fraudulent claims.
fraud_exception.quote: This section shall not apply to fraudulent claims.

rate_submission_audit.limits: Parts markup only (§ 437-56(b)). The manufacturer may make reasonable requests for additional information supporting the submission, and the 90-day effective-date clock starts after receipt. The dealer may change the markup at most once every 12 months. The labor rate (§ 437-28(a)(21)(G)) has no submission or verification procedure.
rate_submission_audit.quote: However, the manufacturer or distributor may make reasonable requests for additional information supporting the submission.

penalties_for_audit_violations.detail: After internal dispute resolution, the dealer may petition DCCA under § 437-51. The manufacturer bears the burden (§ 437-57(b)), and the chargeback is stayed until final judgment. DCCA accepts at most 30 hearing requests per fiscal year, and each party bears its own fees (§ 437-51(b), (g)). Violations are also general license-sanction grounds (§ 437-28(a)(2)), which are not audit-specific.
penalties_for_audit_violations.quote: After the internal dispute resolution process is concluded, the dealer may file a petition in the manner prescribed in section 437-51 protesting the proposed chargeback amount.

states.notes: § 437-57 ('Warranty and incentive audits') covers warranty and incentive audits and chargebacks alike: no audit of paid claims or chargeback more than 1 year after payment; fraud is excepted. Added by L 2010, c 164, and unchanged since. The prior-research scan of 2026 bills found none citing §§ 437-28/56/57.

classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.

cites: Iowa Code § 322A.5(4) (claims, denial grounds, clerical rejection)

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: Not required for chargebacks. Claims must be denied in writing within 30 days (§ 322A.5(4)(a)), but no grounds statement is required.

dealer_response_period.detail: None for chargebacks. A claim rejected for an unintentional clerical-type failure may be resubmitted "in a timely manner" (§ 322A.5(4)(b)); no day count.

clerical_error_protection.detail: A claim may be rejected, but not denied, based solely on an unintentional failure to follow a claim-processing requirement, such as a clerical error, that does not affect legitimacy. The dealer may resubmit a corrected claim. The text addresses claim denial and does not expressly mention post-payment chargebacks.
clerical_error_protection.quote: A franchiser may reject, but shall not deny, a claim based solely on a franchisee's unintentional failure to comply with a specific claim processing requirement, such as a clerical error

documentation_limits.detail: Denial for missing documentation is limited to "the reasonably required documentation".
documentation_limits.quote: the franchisee lacks the reasonably required documentation for the claim

fraud_exception.detail: The 12-month limit does not apply if an Iowa court finds the claim fraudulent. Separately, a claim may be denied on a bona fide belief, based on factual evidence, of an intentionally false or fraudulent statement (§ 322A.5(4)(b)).
fraud_exception.quote: The twelve-month limitation shall not apply if a court of competent jurisdiction in this state finds the claim was fraudulent.

rate_submission_audit.limits: The mfr may audit only the submitted ROs, within 30 days of receiving the submission, and then approve or deny. An approved rate takes effect 45 days after approval. On denial, the dealer may complain to the department, with a hearing before the Department of Inspections, Appeals, and Licensing; the mfr must prove the denial was reasonable. No unduly burdensome methodology (e.g., part-by-part) may be required. The dealer may request a change at most once in any one-year period.
rate_submission_audit.quote: Within thirty days of receiving the franchisee's submission, the franchiser may choose to audit the submitted orders. The franchiser shall then approve or deny the establishment of the franchisee's average percentage markup or labor rate.

penalties_for_audit_violations.detail: Rate submissions only: an unreasonable denial is deemed a violation of ch. 322A, and the department then sets the rate. There is no audit- or chargeback-specific penalty.
penalties_for_audit_violations.quote: If the department of inspections, appeals, and licensing finds the denial was not reasonable, the denial shall be deemed a violation of this chapter

states.notes: Iowa does not phrase this as an audit window. § 322.3(14) bars reducing or disallowing a claim once 12 or more months have passed since the claim was SUBMITTED (not paid). Warranty vs incentive: the same 12-month bar covers warranty parts, repairs and service and "sales or leasing incentives" (rebates, discounted interest rates); ch. 322A.5 claim rules are warranty/recall only. Per § 322A.5(4)(c), the 30-day approval and payment rules do not preclude denials, reductions or chargebacks not otherwise barred by § 322.3(14). No notice, selection, frequency, written-grounds, response, appeal, stay or extrapolation rules. Iowa Code 2026 text read; § 322A.5 history: 2018 ch. 1095, 2021 ch. 38, 2023 ch. 19 (agency rename). Per prior research, 2026 ch. 1057 (HF 2485) amended § 322.3(12) only.

classification.rate_validation_basis: Limited: the manufacturer may check the rate only against the dealer's own submitted ROs (or has no rebuttal right at all), with no right to request additional ROs or run periodic re-verification, and no comparison with other dealers' rates.

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: Silent for chargebacks. A disapproved warranty claim must be disapproved in writing within 30 days (§ 49-1626(5)). A disapproved incentive claim needs written notice with reasons (§ 49-1638(1)). Both govern initial claim review.

dealer_response_period.detail: After a denial or chargeback for a clerical error or administrative technicality, the dealer has 30 days from notice to resubmit (longer if the manufacturer allows). Incentive claims: 60 days (§ 49-1638(3)).
dealer_response_period.quote: A dealer shall have thirty (30) days from the date of notification by a manufacturer or distributor of a denial of a claim or a charge-back to the dealer to resubmit a claim for payment or compensation

internal_appeal.detail: The statute is silent.

chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.detail: There is no chargeback-specific stay. A dealer may protest any dispute arising from a violation of Idaho law after mediation (§ 49-1617(1)(e)). § 49-1617(4)(h) bars the manufacturer from taking 'any other proposed action described in this chapter' until a final decision and exhaustion of appeals. That arguably reaches chargebacks, but it does not say so expressly.
chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.quote: The manufacturer or distributor shall not terminate a dealership, establish a new dealership, relocate a dealership, discontinue an existing franchise, or take any other proposed action described in this chapter until a final decision has been rendered

clerical_error_protection.detail: Warranty: a claim denied or charged back for a clerical error or administrative technicality that does not question its legitimacy may be corrected and resubmitted within 30 days (§ 49-1626(6)-(7)). This is a cure right, not a bar. Incentive: no denial based solely on an incidental failure to meet a claim-processing requirement such as a clerical error (§ 49-1638(2)), with 60 days to resubmit.
clerical_error_protection.quote: A manufacturer shall not deny a claim based solely on a motor vehicle dealer's incidental failure to comply with a specific claim processing requirement, such as a clerical error or other administrative technicality

documentation_limits.detail: Limited. A chargeback needs a completed audit and proof by a preponderance. The documentation ground for incentive claims is limited to the manufacturer's REASONABLE requirements (§ 49-1638(6)(b)). The warranty counterpart (§ 49-1626(9)(b)) says only 'the manufacturer or distributor’s requirements'.
documentation_limits.quote: The claim is unsubstantiated in accordance with the manufacturer's or distributor's reasonable requirements.

fraud_exception.detail: Warranty: the manufacturer may audit for fraudulent claims during any period in which a fraud action may be commenced, and a § 5-218 fraud action is preserved (§ 49-1626(8), (10)). Incentive: chargebacks for fraud are allowed at any time permitted by § 5-218 (§ 49-1638(7)).
fraud_exception.quote: Provided however, that the manufacturer or distributor may audit the dealer for fraudulent claims during any period for which an action for fraud may be commenced.

rate_submission_audit.limits: Within 30 days after receiving the declared schedule, the manufacturer may make reasonable requests for additional supporting information. The 90-day effective-date clock then runs from receipt. It may not require any other methodology or unduly burdensome information, including part-by-part or transaction-by-transaction calculations. The dealer may request a change at most once every 12 months. The retail rate must not be unreasonable compared with same or competitive line franchises in the dealer's area.
rate_submission_audit.quote: within thirty (30) days following receipt of the declared schedule of compensation from the dealer, the manufacturer or distributor may make reasonable requests for additional information supporting the declared schedule of compensation.

states.notes: Warranty (§ 49-1626(8)-(10)): no audit more than 1 year after payment. Chargebacks only after a completed audit and a preponderance showing that the repair was improper, substandard or unnecessary, or the claim unsubstantiated under manufacturer requirements. Incentive (§ 49-1638(5)-(7)): no chargeback of paid claims or prizes and no audit more than 1 year after payment. Chargeback grounds are parallel ('reasonable requirements'), and fraud chargebacks are allowed any time § 5-218 permits. No audit-specific penalty. General protest remedy (§ 49-1617(3)): costs and attorney's fees for a prevailing dealer with pecuniary loss, and treble damages for willful violations. Sections unchanged since 2011 (§ 49-1626) and 2007 (§ 49-1638). The official ch. 16 PDF is current through the 2026 session.

classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: Not required for chargebacks. The written specific-grounds rule in 710/6(b) covers disapproval of submitted claims only.

dealer_response_period.detail: No pre-chargeback response period. The 30-day correct-and-resubmit right in 710/6(b) covers disapproved claims, not chargebacks of paid claims.

clerical_error_protection.detail: Indirect. There is no clerical-error clause, but 710/6(b) bars any debit or chargeback of any warranty RO item absent a finding of fraud or illegal actions by the dealer. Read literally, that also bars clerical-only chargebacks. The same subsection separately lets the mfr charge back "false or unsubstantiated claims"; the statute does not reconcile the two sentences.
clerical_error_protection.quote: No debit reduction or charge back of any item on a warranty repair order may be made absent a finding of fraud or illegal actions by the dealer.

documentation_limits.detail: Mfr may require only "reasonable documentation" for claims.
documentation_limits.quote: The manufacturer or franchiser shall have the right to require reasonable documentation for claims

fraud_exception.detail: After the 1-year window, a fraudulent claim may be charged back only if the mfr proves fraud in an Illinois court.
fraud_exception.quote: the manufacturer retains the right to charge back any fraudulent claim if the manufacturer establishes in a court of competent jurisdiction in this State that the claim is fraudulent

rate_submission_audit.limits: Parts markup: the mfr may audit only the submitted ROs, must do so within 30 days after the declaration, and may adjust the markup based on that audit. The dealer may change the markup at most twice per calendar year, and no unduly burdensome method may be required. Labor rate: the statute gives no audit or rebuttal right. The rate is the effective labor rate on 100 sequential ROs "chosen and submitted by the dealer" (less simple maintenance ROs), and the dealer may request an increase at most once per calendar year.
rate_submission_audit.quote: subject to audit of the submitted repair orders by the motor vehicle franchiser and adjustment of the average percentage markup based on that audit. Any audit must be conducted within 30 days following the declaration.

more_quotes.quote: using the 100 sequential repair orders chosen and submitted by the dealer less simple maintenance repair orders
The dealer may submit a request to the manufacturer for warranty labor rate increases a maximum of once per calendar year.

states.notes: Audit window: 1 year from the date the claim was paid or credit issued; chargeback of "false or unsubstantiated claims". Warranty vs incentive: the same 1-year audit and chargeback rule expressly applies to "all other incentive and reimbursement programs"; there are no separate incentive procedures. The statute has no notice, selection, frequency, appeal, stay or extrapolation rules. Confidence is medium only because the fraud-only chargeback sentence conflicts with the false-or-unsubstantiated chargeback right; the rest reads plainly. Pending: SB1939 (104th GA) would amend 710/6, but its audit and chargeback text is unchanged; it passed the Senate and has sat in House Rules since 3/20/2026. No audit-specific penalty.
