cites: Ind. Code § 9-32-13-15.5 (retail rate submission, rebuttal, annual audit)

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: Written notice of the specific grounds for each claim charged back after an audit. On the dealer's written request, the mfr must hold a meeting (in person, video or phone) or give a written explanation, and must respond with all details supporting each chargeback. The notice is tied to the chargeback itself, not to a proposed chargeback.
written_reasons_before_chargeback.quote: A manufacturer or distributor shall provide a dealer with written notification of the specific grounds upon which a claim is being charged back as a result of an audit.

dealer_response_period.detail: At least 30 days after receiving the chargeback notice to submit documentation or information rebutting it. If the chargeback rests on documentation, material claim-submission or other material clerical noncompliance, the dealer also has 30 days from receipt to cure; the parties may agree to extend the cure time for high volumes.
dealer_response_period.quote: allowing the dealer at least thirty (30) days after receipt of the notice of charge back to provide additional supporting documentation or information rebutting the charge back

internal_appeal.detail: Mfr must provide a "reasonable appeals process". The dealer or its designated agent, officer or employee may request in writing a meeting (in person, video or phone) or a written explanation of the basis for a chargeback.
internal_appeal.quote: A manufacturer or distributor shall provide a reasonable appeals process allowing the dealer at least thirty (30) days after receipt of the notice of charge back

chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.detail: Not stated. The § 17(d) appeal runs after the notice of chargeback.

clerical_error_protection.detail: No denial based solely on an incidental failure to meet a specific claim-processing requirement, including a clerical error or administrative technicality that does not question legitimacy, if the dealer gives reasonably sufficient documentation of a good-faith attempt to comply (§ 17(c)). Audit chargebacks based on documentation or material clerical noncompliance carry a 30-day cure right (§ 17(d)). A missing required signature is not a clerical error (§ 17(e)).
clerical_error_protection.quote: may not deny a claim based solely on a motor vehicle dealer's incidental failure to comply with a specific claim processing requirement, including a clerical error or other administrative technicality

documentation_limits.detail: A substantiation chargeback is allowed only where the dealer failed to substantiate the claim under the mfr's written procedures "or other reasonable means".
documentation_limits.quote: claim that the dealer failed to substantiate in accordance with the manufacturer's written procedures or other reasonable means

fraud_exception.detail: The 12-month audit and chargeback limit does not apply if the mfr can prove fraud on a claim. No outer limit is stated.
fraud_exception.quote: However, the limitations of this subsection do not apply if the manufacturer or distributor can prove fraud on a claim.

rate_submission_audit.limits: Rebuttal due within 60 days after receipt of the declaration. It must substantiate how the declaration is unreasonable or materially inaccurate, propose an adjusted rate and give written support. With no timely rebuttal, the rate is established. The mfr may perform annual audits to verify the dealer's effective rates have not decreased, and if they have, may reduce the rate prospectively only. The dealer may declare at most once per 12 months, and no unduly burdensome method may be required. The dealer may complain to the Secretary of State dealer services division within 30 days of the rebuttal. The prior rate stays in effect until 30 days after a final court decision and all appeals.
rate_submission_audit.quote: A manufacturer or distributor may perform annual audits to verify that a dealer's effective rates have not decreased.

more_quotes.quote: A manufacturer or distributor may challenge the dealer's declaration by submitting a rebuttal not later than sixty (60) days after the date the declaration was received.

the rebuttal must substantiate how the dealer's declaration is unreasonable or materially inaccurate. The rebuttal must propose an adjusted retail rate and provide written support for the proposed adjustments.

states.notes: Audit and chargeback window: up to 12 months after payment (§ 17(b)). Chargeback grounds: false or fraudulent, repairs not properly made, work not necessary, or claim not substantiated. No discrimination among dealers in auditing or charging back (§ 17(b)). Warranty vs incentive: § 17 covers dealer claims for delivery and prep, warranty work and incentive payments (§ 17(a)(1)), so the same audit, notice, appeal and cure procedure applies to incentive audits. The chargeback grounds are warranty-oriented. Incentive claims may be amended or supplemented within 60 days of submission, possible submission, or chargeback (§ 17(e)). No notice-before-audit, selection-basis, frequency or extrapolation rule. Amendments: § 17 last amended P.L.134-2023; P.L.92-2025 (eff. 7/1/2025) deleted the pre-complaint mediation-demand sentence from § 15.5(e). § 15.5 does not apply to manufactured housing, heavy-duty vocational vehicles or RVs. New RV chapter (P.L.42-2025): IC 9-32-19-29(g) lets a warrantor "conduct a warranty audit of a recreational vehicle dealer's records on a reasonable basis." No audit-specific penalty. Failures under § 17(a) are "unfair practices", with complaints under IC 9-32-13-31.

classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: No notice-content rule. The mfr's claim for reimbursement after an audit must be presented to the dealer within 90 days of the audit of the item (see notes).

internal_appeal.detail: Not required. The statute refers to "any challenge or appeal by either party" of an audit (see stay) but does not require the mfr to offer one.

chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.detail: The mfr may not set off or take control of dealer funds (or funds in an account designated for the dealer) based on audit findings until a final decision is issued on any challenge or appeal of the audit or claim by either party.
chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.quote: may not setoff or otherwise take control over funds … based upon the findings of an audit or other claim with respect thereto until a final decision is issued with respect to any challenge or appeal

clerical_error_protection.detail: A dealer's failure to follow specific claim-processing requirements is not grounds for denial or reduction if the dealer presents reasonable documentation or other evidence substantiating the claim.
clerical_error_protection.quote: failure to comply with the specific requirements of processing a claim may not constitute grounds for denial of the claim or reduction of the amount of compensation paid to the dealer if the dealer presents reasonable documentation

documentation_limits.detail: No unreasonable proof may be required. A reasonably substantiated claim may not be divided or reduced.
documentation_limits.quote: shall not require unreasonable proof to establish compensation under this section … A claim for compensation shall not be divided or the amount to be reimbursed reduced if the new vehicle dealer has reasonably substantiated the claim.

fraud_exception.detail: With evidence of fraud, the mfr may audit for longer periods and charge back fraudulent claims, subject to the K.S.A. 60-513(a)(3) limitation period.
fraud_exception.quote: If there is evidence of fraud, this subsection does not limit the right of the manufacturer to audit for longer periods and chargeback for any fraudulent claim, subject to the limitation period under K.S.A. 60-513(a)(3)

rate_submission_audit.limits: The mfr may audit only the submitted ROs, within 30 days of receiving the submission, and then approve or deny. An approved rate takes effect 45 days after approval. On denial, the dealer may complain to the director of vehicles, with a hearing under K.S.A. 8-2411; the mfr must prove the denial was reasonable. No unduly burdensome methodology may be required. The dealer may request a change at most once in any one-year period.
rate_submission_audit.quote: Within 30 days of receiving the dealer's submission, the first or second stage manufacturer or distributor may choose to audit the submitted orders.

penalties_for_audit_violations.detail: An unreasonable rate denial "shall be deemed a violation of this section", and the director of vehicles then sets the rate. The whole section, including the audit, chargeback and setoff limits, is enforceable under K.S.A. 8-2411.
penalties_for_audit_violations.quote: If the director of vehicles finds that the denial was not reasonable, the denial shall be deemed a violation of this section

more_quotes.quote: This section may be enforced pursuant to K.S.A. 8-2411, and amendments thereto.

states.notes: Warranty vs incentive: two parallel but identical 1-year audit rights, each running from payment, with chargeback only for "false or unsubstantiated" claims (8-2415(e)). The 90-day presentment, setoff stay and fraud extension apply to both. The mfr's reimbursement claim must be presented within 90 days of the audit of the item: "A claim for reimbursement by the first or second stage manufacturer or distributor of sums due following an audit must be presented to the dealer within 90 days of the audit of the item subject to the claim." No notice-before-audit, selection, frequency, written-grounds, response-period, appeal-process or extrapolation rules. History: L. 1980 ch. 36 § 15 ... L. 2019 ch. 5 § 1 (SB 39), eff. 7/1/2019. Per prior research, no 2025-2026 amendment was found.

classification.rate_validation_basis: Limited: the manufacturer may check the rate only against the dealer's own submitted ROs (or has no rebuttal right at all), with no right to request additional ROs or run periodic re-verification, and no comparison with other dealers' rates.

cites: KRS 190.046(7) (audit window, documentation, pre-chargeback notice, fraud)

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: Before requiring any chargeback, reimbursement or credit against a future transaction arising from an audit, the mfr must give the dealer written notice with a copy of its audit and the detailed reason for each intended chargeback.
written_reasons_before_chargeback.quote: Prior to requiring any charge-back … arising out of an audit, the manufacturer or distributor shall submit written notice to the dealer along with a copy of its audit and the detailed reason for each intended charge-back

dealer_response_period.detail: Business days. If incomplete, inaccurate or missing information is found during an audit, the mfr must promptly notify the dealer and extend the time to submit by a reasonable period of at least 5 business days after notice. There is no general rebuttal period before a chargeback.
dealer_response_period.quote: if incomplete, inaccurate, or missing information is discovered during an audit, then the manufacturer or distributor shall promptly notify the dealer … not less than five (5) business days following notice

internal_appeal.detail: Not required. Disputes go to a hearing under KRS 190.057 (KRS Chapter 13B) per KRS 190.046(3)(f).

clerical_error_protection.detail: Failure to meet the mfr's specific claim-processing requirements is not grounds for denial or reduction if the dealer presents reasonable documentation or other evidence substantiating the claim.
clerical_error_protection.quote: A dealer's failure to comply with the specific requirements of the manufacturer or distributor for processing a claim may not constitute grounds for denial of the claim or reduction of the amount of compensation paid

documentation_limits.detail: No documentation may be required for warranty, recall, sales or incentive claims more than 12 months after payment or the end of a program of 1 year or less, whichever is later (7)(b). No unreasonable proof may be required to establish reasonable compensation (2)(e). The dealer need not keep defective parts more than 30 days after payment (3)(e).
documentation_limits.quote: A manufacturer or distributor shall not require documentation for warranty, recall, sales, or incentive claims more than twelve (12) months after the claim was paid

fraud_exception.detail: If the mfr has evidence that would lead a person of ordinary caution to believe a claim was fraudulent, false or misleading, it may audit during any period in which a fraud or false-claims action may be brought under state law.
fraud_exception.quote: a manufacturer that possesses evidence which would cause a person of ordinary caution, prudence, and judgment to believe that a dealer submitted a claim that was fraudulent, false, or misleading may audit the dealer

rate_submission_audit.limits: No retail-rate submission, audit or verification procedure in the statute. "Reasonable compensation" rests mainly on what the dealer charges other customers. It may not be less than the dealer's retail charge for like services and parts, with a parts minimum of cost plus 30% gross profit (KRS 190.046(2)(a), (c)).
rate_submission_audit.quote: the principal factor to be considered shall be the amount of money that the dealer is charging its other customers for the same type service or repair work

states.notes: Audit window: 12 months after payment or the end of a program of 1 year or less, whichever is later (7)(a). Warranty vs incentive: one procedure. (7) expressly covers "warranty, recall, sales, or incentive claims", and the documentation cutoff, pre-chargeback notice and fraud rule apply equally. No notice-before-audit, selection-basis, frequency, appeal, stay or extrapolation rules. Amendments: the official page shows the version effective 7/15/2026, from 2026 Ky. Acts ch. 83 (HB 648). Per the LRC enacted summary, that act rewrote only the Class 7+ heavy-truck compensation rules in (2)(d) (including a 90-day minimum claim-submission window) and did not address audits. No audit-specific penalty. General fine for violating KRS 190.010-190.080: $25-$500 (KRS 190.990(1)).

classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.

audit_frequency_limit.limit: No more than 2 sales-related and 2 service-related audits in any 12-month period. Routine claim reviews in the normal course of business are not limited.
audit_frequency_limit.quote: It shall be deemed an unfair act pursuant to this Chapter to audit a dealer more frequently than two sales-related and two service-related audits in a twelve-month period.
audit_frequency_limit.score_level_reason: Up to two service-related audits in any 12-month period.

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: Not required for chargebacks. Written grounds are required only for disapproval of submitted claims (A)(14).

dealer_response_period.detail: Not counted as a response period: the only window in the statute is to protest to a board, sue, or (LA) correct incentive/sales data. Incentive and sales audits only: the dealer must be allowed at least 120 days from the program period to correct sales data. No response period for warranty chargebacks.
dealer_response_period.quote: In no event shall the manufacturer, distributor, distributor branch, or factory branch fail to allow the dealer to make corrections to the sales data in less than one hundred twenty days from the program period.

clerical_error_protection.detail: No denial based solely on an incidental failure to meet a specific claim-processing requirement, a clerical error, or another administrative technicality.
clerical_error_protection.quote: A manufacturer or distributor shall not deny a claim solely based on a dealer's incidental failure to comply with a specific claim processing requirement, or a clerical error, or other administrative technicality.

documentation_limits.detail: A substantiation chargeback may rest only on reasonable written requirements that the dealer was told about before the claim arose and that were in effect then (B)(2)(d). No chargeback where the dealer shows the repair resolved the presented condition and documents the repair and its process (B)(4)(a); this does not apply to recreational products dealers. No audit liability for failing to keep parts more than 6 months (B)(1). No chargeback of a consumer rebate where the dealer relied in good faith on the consumer's qualifying information and followed program guidelines (B)(8).
documentation_limits.quote: The dealer failed to reasonably substantiate the repair in accordance with reasonable written requirements of the manufacturer or distributor, if the dealer was notified of the requirements prior to the time the claim arose

more_quotes.quote: A dealer shall not be charged back on a claim when a dealer performs a repair covered by the manufacturer's or distributor's warranty, and the dealer reasonably demonstrates that the repair resolved the condition

fraud_exception.detail: The audit and chargeback limits (warranty and incentive) do not apply to intentionally false or fraudulent claims. No outer limit is stated.
fraud_exception.quote: Limitations on warranty parts or service compensation, sales incentive audits, rebates, or other forms of incentive compensation, chargebacks for warranty parts or service compensation … shall not be effective in the case of intentionally false or fraudulent claims.

rate_submission_audit.limits: The submitted rate is presumed accurate and takes effect 45 days after receipt unless rebutted within 45 days. If the calculated rate is substantially higher or lower than the rate on record, the mfr may request in writing, within 45 days, additional ROs for the 30 days before or after the submitted period. It then has 45 days from receipt to rebut, using the same RO rules and exclusions. A rebuttal must reasonably substantiate material inaccuracy, explain every reason with evidence, include all calculations, and propose an adjusted rate based on the dealer's qualifying ROs. Only one rebuttal is allowed, with no later changes unless new information could not have been known. The dealer may protest to the Louisiana Motor Vehicle Commission within 60 days; the mfr must prove material inaccuracy by a preponderance. A dealer win is retroactive to day 45. The dealer may submit at most once per 12 months.
rate_submission_audit.quote: may request in writing, within forty-five days of receipt of the submitted parts mark-up or labor rate, additional repair orders for a period of either thirty days prior to or thirty days subsequent to the time

more_quotes.quote: shall not submit more than one rebuttal to the dealer and shall not add to, expand, supplement, or otherwise modify any element
Reasonably substantiating that the submission is materially inaccurate and by providing a full explanation of any and all reasons.

penalties_for_audit_violations.detail: Auditing more often than 2 sales-related and 2 service-related audits in 12 months is "deemed an unfair act" under the Chapter, which the Louisiana Motor Vehicle Commission enforces. In incentive audits, the dealer owes no penalty beyond amounts advanced on a vehicle reported incorrectly; it is charged back the amount reported incorrectly and credited with any amount due on the actual sale date.
penalties_for_audit_violations.quote: no penalty other than amounts advanced on a vehicle reported incorrectly shall be due in connection with the audit

states.notes: Warranty audit window: the 12 months immediately after claim payment. Incentive audit window: the 12 months after final payment under the promotion or program (B)(1). Chargeback grounds (B)(2): false or fraudulent, not properly made, unnecessary under accepted workmanship standards, or unsubstantiated under reasonable pre-notified written requirements. Warranty vs incentive: separate windows. The 120-day sales-data correction right and the no-penalty rule are incentive-only. The frequency cap counts sales-related and service-related audits separately (2 each per 12 months). No notice, selection, written-grounds-before-chargeback, appeal, stay or extrapolation rules. § 1262 does not apply to marine, motorcycle/ATV or RV dealers (C). The official text shows history through Acts 2021, No. 76; per prior research, no 2025-2026 act amending § 1262 was found.

classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.
classification.audit_consequence_basis: Auditing more often than 2 sales-related and 2 service-related audits in 12 months is "deemed an unfair act" under the Chapter, which the Louisiana Motor Vehicle Commission enforces. In incentive audits, the dealer owes no penalty beyond amounts advanced on a vehicle reported incorrectly; it is charged back the amount reported incorrectly and credited with any amount due on the actual sale date.

cites: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 93B, § 9(c)-(i) (audits, chargebacks, meeting, extrapolation, retaliation)

selection_basis_disclosed.detail: At the required pre-chargeback meeting, the mfr must give a written statement of the basis on which the dealer was selected for audit or review.
selection_basis_disclosed.quote: a written statement containing the basis upon which the motor vehicle dealer was selected for audit or review

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: Before any chargeback, the mfr must meet the dealer (in person, video or teleconference) and give a detailed explanation, with supporting documentation, of the basis for each proposed chargeback. Written audit results must be given no later than the chargeback (h). The basis may not change after the audit unless new information arises, and then the dealer gets a new meeting and response right.
written_reasons_before_chargeback.quote: At such meeting the manufacturer or distributor shall provide a detailed explanation, with supporting documentation, as to the basis for each of the claims for which the manufacturer or distributor proposed a chargeback

more_quotes.quote: The results of each audit or examination shall be compiled in writing and a copy shall be timely provided to the motor vehicle dealer not later than the time that any charge back occurs.

dealer_response_period.detail: A reasonable period after the meeting, matched to the volume of claims, but never less than 30 days.
dealer_response_period.quote: a reasonable period of time after the meeting within which to respond to the proposed chargebacks, with such period to be commensurate with the volume of claims under consideration, but in no case less than 30 days after the meeting

internal_appeal.detail: Not counted: § 9 requires a pre-chargeback meeting and a 30-day response period, and the dealer may protest the results, but the statute does not require the manufacturer to offer an internal appeal. Mandatory pre-chargeback meeting plus a response period of at least 30 days (§ 9(e)). An unexcused dealer failure to schedule or attend a meeting it agreed to relieves the mfr of these duties; excused absences are listed. The dealer may also "protest the results of the audit, including the manner in which it was conducted" (§ 9(h)); the forum is not specified.
internal_appeal.quote: A manufacturer or distributor shall not chargeback a motor vehicle dealer subsequent to the payment of a claim unless a representative of the manufacturer or distributor first meets in person or by video or teleconference

chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.detail: No stay pending a protest, but no chargeback may occur before the § 9(e) meeting.

extrapolation.detail: A discrepancy for any period may not be determined, in whole or in part, by extrapolating results from a prior or subsequent period without the dealer's consent. Sampling within the audited period is not addressed.
extrapolation.quote: the amount of a discrepancy for any period shall not be determined in whole or in part by extrapolating audit or examination results from a prior or subsequent period without the consent of the dealer

documentation_limits.detail: A noncompliance chargeback may rest only on the mfr's reasonable written requirements in effect when the claim was presented for payment (warranty (d); incentive (e)). Dealers need not keep defective parts more than 90 days after claim submission (§ 9(b)(4)).
documentation_limits.quote: the motor vehicle dealer failed to comply with the reasonable written requirements of the manufacturer or distributor in effect at the time the claim was presented for payment

fraud_exception.detail: With evidence of fraud or fraudulent concealment, the mfr may audit records for periods over 1 year. No cap is stated.
fraud_exception.quote: If there is evidence of fraud or if there has been fraudulent concealment, said manufacturer or distributor shall have a right to audit records for periods exceeding 1 year.

rate_submission_audit.limits: Parts and labor: the declared rate is presumed fair and reasonable and takes effect 30 days after declaration, subject to audit of the submitted ROs and a rebuttal. If rebutted, the mfr must propose an adjusted rate no later than 30 days after submission. The dealer may sue within 30 days of the proposal, and the mfr must prove the declared rate inaccurate or unreasonable. No unduly burdensome method may be required. The dealer may declare at most once per calendar year. Parts only: an agreed markup may be used instead if agreed within 30 days of the dealer's written request.
rate_submission_audit.quote: The average labor rate shall go into effect 30 days following the declaration, subject to audit of the submitted repair orders by the franchisor and a rebuttal of the declared rate.

more_quotes.quote: If the declared rate is rebutted, the manufacturer or distributor shall propose an adjustment of the average percentage markup based on the rebuttal not later than 30 days after submission.

penalties_for_audit_violations.detail: Auditing or examining a dealer's sales or service accounts as retribution for exercising rights under ch. 93B or the franchise agreement violates § 3(a).
penalties_for_audit_violations.quote: It shall be a violation of subsection (a) of section 3 for any manufacturer or distributor to audit or examine any sales or service account or activity of a motor vehicle dealer as retribution

states.notes: Audit window: 1 year after payment or the end of the program period, whichever is later, for warranty, parts-recall and sales incentive/bonus claims (§ 9(c)). Warranty vs incentive: same window and procedure (meeting, selection basis, 30-day response, no cross-period extrapolation, written results, anti-retaliation), but different chargeback grounds. Warranty (d): fraudulent or false, repairs improper or unnecessary, or failure to meet reasonable written requirements. Incentive (e): fraudulent or false, sales not made, sales not timely, or failure to meet reasonable written requirements. Incentive claims may be filed within 6 months after the retail sale or the end of the program (§ 9(j)). Auditors must use best efforts not to unreasonably interfere with dealer business, and audits must finish within a reasonable time (§ 9(f)). No clerical-error rule and no numeric frequency cap. Last amended St. 2012, c. 152. H4019 (194th) was sent to study on 4/2/2026 and formal sessions ended 7/31/2026, so there is no 2025-2026 change.

classification.rate_validation_basis: Limited: the manufacturer may check the rate only against the dealer's own submitted ROs (or has no rebuttal right at all), with no right to request additional ROs or run periodic re-verification, and no comparison with other dealers' rates.
classification.audit_consequence_basis: Auditing or examining a dealer's sales or service accounts as retribution for exercising rights under ch. 93B or the franchise agreement violates § 3(a).

cites: Md. Code, Transp. § 15-212(c)(3), (6)-(7) (rate submission, rebuttal, verification, audit ban)

extrapolation.detail: No sampling rule. Audits must be conducted under generally accepted accounting principles ((c)(11)(iii)).

clerical_error_protection.detail: Failure to comply with a specific mfr requirement is not grounds for denial or reduction if the dealer presents documentation or other reasonable evidence that the repair and claim followed warranty guidelines.
clerical_error_protection.quote: A dealer's failure to comply with a specific requirement of the manufacturer or distributor may not constitute grounds for denial of the claim or reduction of the amount of compensation paid to the dealer if the dealer presents documentation

documentation_limits.detail: The dealer may substantiate with "documentation or other reasonable evidence" ((c)(10)). No denial, reduction or chargeback for properly performed covered warranty or required recall repairs, including repairs found during a separate customer-requested repair or through a recall notice ((c)(14)).
documentation_limits.quote: A licensee may not deny a claim, reduce the amount of compensation to a dealer, or process a charge back to a dealer for performing covered warranty or required recall repairs on a vehicle

fraud_exception.detail: The 9-month chargeback limit does not limit the right to audit any claim or to charge back any claim proven fraudulent. No outer limit is stated.
fraud_exception.quote: This paragraph does not limit the right of a manufacturer or distributor to: 1. Conduct an audit of any claim filed under this section; or 2. Charge back for any claim that is proven to be fraudulent.

rate_submission_audit.limits: The submission is presumed accurate and reasonable. The licensee must approve or rebut within 30 days; a rebuttal must consist of reasonable substantiating evidence that the declared rate is materially inaccurate. Otherwise the rate takes effect on day 31. In any action the only issue is material inaccuracy, and the licensee bears the burden. The licensee may verify the dealer's effective rates once a year and adjust prospectively, up or down. It may not calculate its own rate by any other method or use the dealer's or other dealers' warranty compensation data. It may not conduct any warranty, retail-repair or other service-related audit solely because the dealer requests retail-rate reimbursement. The dealer may submit at most once a year; corrections are not a new submission.
rate_submission_audit.quote: A licensee may verify a dealer's effective rates once annually.

more_quotes.quote: Consist of reasonable substantiating evidence that the declared rate is materially inaccurate.

Conduct any warranty or retail customer repair audit, or other service-related audit, solely because the dealer makes a request for warranty reimbursement at retail rates in the ordinary course of business

penalties_for_audit_violations.detail: The ban on audits triggered solely by a retail-rate request ((c)(7)(v)) is enforced through general remedies. The MVA Administrator may fine up to $50,000 per violation of the subtitle and order compensation (§ 15-212(d)), and injured persons may recover damages and attorney fees (§ 15-213). There is no audit-specific penalty amount.
penalties_for_audit_violations.quote: May order the licensee to pay a fine not exceeding $50,000 for each violation of this subtitle

states.notes: Chargeback window: 9 months from payment or credit, only for claims the mfr shows are false or unsubstantiated ((c)(11)(i)). Warranty vs incentive: § 15-212(c) covers warranty and recall claims only. No incentive-audit or incentive-chargeback provision was found in §§ 15-201 and 15-206 through 15-216 (searched for "audit"/"charge back"). No notice, selection, frequency, written-grounds, response, appeal, stay or extrapolation rules. Compensation policies must be applied uniformly among in-state dealers ((c)(7)(vi)). Last substantive change: 2016 ch. 720; 2020 ch. 628 was a corrective fix. 2026: Md. Laws ch. 463 (SB 345/HB 1214), effective 10/1/2026, amends §§ 15-201 and 15-214 so dealer and manufacturer associations may request an MVA administrative hearing to resolve disputes or get interpretations of the franchise law, including § 15-212. It does not change § 15-212's text.

classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.
classification.audit_consequence_basis: The ban on audits triggered solely by a retail-rate request ((c)(7)(v)) is enforced through general remedies. 10 M.R.S. § 1176 (warranty; parts markup submission and audit; claims)

advance_notice.detail: Not required. For incentive audits, the 12-month lookback is counted from "the date notifying the dealer that an audit is to be conducted". That presupposes a notice but sets no timing or form.
advance_notice.quote: Audits of incentive payments may be only for the 12-month period immediately preceding the date notifying the dealer that an audit is to be conducted.

audit_frequency_limit.quote: A manufacturer may reasonably and periodically audit a new motor vehicle dealer to determine the validity of paid claims or any charge-backs for customer or dealer incentives.
audit_frequency_limit.detail: Qualitative only (e.g., "reasonable" or "periodic" audits); no numeric cap. Qualitative only: audits must be reasonable and periodic. No numeric cap.

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: Not required for chargebacks. Written specific reasons are required for disapproval of submitted claims within 60 days (§ 1176).

clerical_error_protection.detail: Covers warranty claims (§ 1176) and paid claims and customer/dealer incentives (§ 1176-A). Elements based on an incidental failure, clerical error or other technicality may not be denied, even if other elements are contested, as long as the dealer corrects the error under licensee guidelines.
clerical_error_protection.quote: A franchisor may not deny those elements of a paid claim or customer or dealer incentive that are based on a dealer's incidental failure to comply with a claim requirement or a clerical error or other technicality

more_quotes.quote: A franchisor may not deny those elements of a warranty claim that are based on a dealer's incidental failure to comply with a claim requirement or a clerical error or other technicality

fraud_exception.detail: No fraud carve-out. The statute sets no lookback for warranty paid-claim audits at all, so there is nothing to extend.

rate_submission_audit.limits: Parts markup: the declared markup takes effect 30 days after declaration, subject to audit of the submitted ROs and adjustment based on that audit. The audit is limited to the submitted ROs, and no deadline is set. No unduly burdensome method or information (e.g., part-by-part or transaction-by-transaction) may be required. The dealer may change the markup at most twice per calendar year. Labor: the statute gives no audit or validation right. The mfr must pay the dealer's customary retail labor rate if that rate is routinely posted conspicuously for service customers.
rate_submission_audit.quote: goes into effect 30 days following the declaration, subject to audit of the submitted repair orders by the franchisor and adjustment of the average percentage markup based on that audit

states.notes: Maine sets NO lookback for warranty paid-claim audits. The only express time limit is the 12-month lookback for incentive-payment audits, counted back from the audit-notice date (§ 1176-A). Warranty vs incentive: the same "reasonably and periodically" audit right and clerical-error rule cover both; only incentive audits have the 12-month lookback. No selection, written-grounds, response, appeal, stay, extrapolation or documentation rules. § 1176 awards costs and attorney fees when a dealer successfully sues to collect a disapproved claim. § 1174(3)(C-4)(3) bars chargebacks or incentive reductions in response to stop-sale/do-not-drive used-vehicle compensation claims. The Revisor text is current through data extracted 10/20/2025; § 1176-A was last amended by PL 2017, c. 217, § 8. 2026 check: PL 2025, c. 592 (LD 2104, signed 3/23/2026) rewrote 10 M.R.S. § 1248 for personal sports mobile dealers (a separate chapter, with no audit text) and did not touch §§ 1176/1176-A. classification.rate_validation_basis: Limited: the manufacturer may check the rate only against the dealer's own submitted ROs (or has no rebuttal right at all), with no right to request additional ROs or run periodic re-verification, and no comparison with other dealers' rates.

cites: Mich. Comp. Laws § 445.1577a(2) (rate submission, additional ROs, contest)

selection_basis_disclosed.detail: If a pre-chargeback meeting is held, the mfr must give a written statement of the basis on which the claims were selected for audit or review. It need not disclose proprietary or confidential customer or other-dealer information, or information whose disclosure is prohibited by law. No statement is required if the mfr instead answers the dealer's written information request in writing.
selection_basis_disclosed.quote: a written statement containing the basis on which the claim or claims of the dealer were selected for audit or review by the manufacturer

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: At the meeting, a detailed explanation with supporting documentation of the basis for each proposed chargeback. The alternative precondition is a written response to the dealer's written request for information.
written_reasons_before_chargeback.quote: At the meeting, the manufacturer shall provide a detailed explanation, with supporting documentation, of the basis for each proposed chargeback of a claim to the dealer

dealer_response_period.detail: At least 45 days after the meeting to respond to proposed chargebacks, longer if the volume warrants. Separately, for chargebacks on false, unsubstantiated, missing-documentation, or improper diagnosis or repair grounds, the dealer has 14 days after receiving the chargeback notice to supply documentation meeting the mfr's requirements. If the claim is then valid, it may not be charged back ((5)).
dealer_response_period.quote: the manufacturer shall provide the motor vehicle dealer's representative a reasonable period of time of at least 45 days to respond to the proposed chargebacks

more_quotes.quote: a new motor vehicle dealer has 14 days after the date the new motor vehicle dealer receives notice of the chargeback to supply documentation that meets the manufacturer's requirements to support the validity of the claim

internal_appeal.detail: Pre-chargeback meeting (in person, video or telephone) with a dealer-designated officer or employee, or a written response to the dealer's written request for information. After a meeting, the dealer gets at least 45 days to respond. An unexcused dealer failure or refusal to schedule, attend or take part relieves the mfr.
internal_appeal.quote: A manufacturer may not charge a claim back to a new motor vehicle dealer after the claim is paid unless a representative of the manufacturer first meets in person or by video teleconference or telephone

chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.detail: Not stated beyond the meeting/written-response precondition in (10).

clerical_error_protection.detail: No denial for an incidental failure to follow a specific claim-processing requirement, such as a clerical error, that does not question legitimacy. The text addresses denial; post-payment chargebacks are governed by (4)-(5).
clerical_error_protection.quote: may not deny a claim made under this section because of a new motor vehicle dealer's incidental failure to comply with a specific claim processing requirement, such as a clerical error, that does not call into question the legitimacy

documentation_limits.detail: None. "Lacks proper documentation" is itself a chargeback ground ((4)(b)). The dealer must keep warranty repair records, including employee time records, for at least 2 years after payment ((7)).

fraud_exception.detail: Fraudulent claims may be charged back up to 6 years after payment, versus 12 months for the other grounds.
fraud_exception.quote: The manufacturer shows that the claim is fraudulent. However, the manufacturer may not charge back the amount paid if the claim is found to be fraudulent more than 6 years after payment.

rate_submission_audit.limits: The mfr must approve or disapprove within 45 days; otherwise the rate is deemed approved. If the calculated parts or labor rate is substantially higher or lower than the rate on record, the mfr may request additional documentation for the 60 days before or after the submitted period. A contest must come within 45 days and reasonably substantiate that the rate is inaccurate, incomplete or unreasonable compared with the retail rates of similarly situated same-line-make Michigan dealers in a comparable area. It must include a written explanation and a proposed adjustment. Internal dispute resolution, if available, must finish within 45 days; the dealer may then sue in circuit court, and the mfr bears the burden. The dealer may declare at most once per calendar year. No unduly burdensome method may be required. The procedure applies when the dealer demands warranty pay above agreed rates.
rate_submission_audit.quote: the manufacturer may request additional documentation for a period of either 60 days before or 60 days after the time period for which the repair orders were submitted for purposes of an adjustment

more_quotes.quote: by reasonably substantiating that the rate is inaccurate, incomplete, or unreasonable in light of the factors described in subsection (1)

states.notes: Chargeback windows run from payment: 12 months for false, unsubstantiated, missing-documentation or improper diagnosis/repair grounds, and 6 years for fraud ((4)). Audits are allowed only within those periods ((11)). Warranty vs incentive: promotion/incentive claims may be charged back only under (4) ((9)), and (10)-(11) cover warranty and promotion claims, so the procedure is the same. Incentive claims must be paid within 15 days of approval ((9)). The mfr may not limit incentive access or vehicle/parts allocation solely because the dealer exercises § 17a rate rights (445.1577a(6)). No notice-before-audit, frequency or extrapolation rules. Last amended 2018 PA 668 (eff. 3/28/2019). Per the 9/25/2026 watchlist check, there is no 2025-2026 amendment. No audit-specific penalty; general remedies are in MCL 445.1580-445.1581.

classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.

cites: Minn. Stat. § 80E.041, subd. 8 (claims, audit, chargeback, clerical resubmission)

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: Not required for chargebacks. Claims must be "specifically disapproved in writing" within 30 days (subd. 8(a)).

dealer_response_period.detail: Only for denials or chargebacks based solely on an incidental processing failure, clerical error or administrative technicality: the dealer may resubmit under reasonable guidelines within 30 days after notice. No general rebuttal period.
dealer_response_period.quote: The manufacturer shall allow the dealer to resubmit the claim according to reasonable guidelines not later than 30 days after the dealer receives notice of the initial claim denial or charge back.

internal_appeal.detail: Not required for chargebacks. Rate disputes use the mfr's internal dispute resolution procedure "if any" (subds. 2(c), 4(c)).

clerical_error_protection.detail: No denial and no chargeback of a claim or payment based solely on an incidental processing failure, clerical error or administrative technicality that does not question legitimacy. The dealer has a 30-day resubmission right. This expressly covers chargebacks.
clerical_error_protection.quote: A manufacturer shall not deny a claim submitted under this section or charge back a claim or payment based solely on the dealer's incidental failure to comply with a claim processing procedure, a clerical error, or other administrative technicality

fraud_exception.detail: No separate fraud window. The single 1-year audit right covers both "not reasonably substantiated" and "fraudulent" claims.

rate_submission_audit.limits: No express right to audit ROs or request more ROs. The mfr may disapprove a parts or labor rate only in writing, within 30 days of submission, with reasonable substantiation that the submission is inaccurate, incomplete or unreasonable compared with the retail rate of similarly situated same-line-make dealers in a comparable Minnesota area. If the mfr has fewer than 5 in-state dealers, the comparison may use U.S. dealers (subd. 7). It must propose an adjustment. With no timely response, the rate is approved. Disagreements go to the mfr's internal dispute resolution (if any), then a civil suit under § 80E.17 within 60 days. The dealer may establish a rate at most once per year (subd. 5).
rate_submission_audit.quote: the disapproval includes a reasonable substantiation that the retail rate submission is inaccurate, incomplete, or unreasonable in light of a comparison to the retail rate charged by other similarly situated franchised motor vehicle dealers
rate_submission_audit.pinpoint: Minn. Stat. § 80E.041, subd. 2(b)(3); same for labor, subd. 4(b)(3)

states.notes: Audit right: "a period of one year", with no start date stated. Chargebacks only for claims "not reasonably substantiated or fraudulent", and the mfr bears the burden of proof (subd. 8(a)): "The manufacturer has the burden of proving that a claim is not reasonably substantiated or fraudulent." Warranty vs incentive: the same audit, chargeback and clerical rules apply to "all other incentive and reimbursement programs that are subject to audit by the manufacturer" (subd. 8(b)). § 80E.045 subd. 4 bars chargebacks or incentive reductions solely because a dealer filed a recall/stop-sale claim, "Subject to the audit provisions of section 80E.041". Cost recovery requires 60 days' advance written notice (subd. 6). No notice-before-audit, selection, frequency, written-grounds, appeal, stay or extrapolation rules. Last amended 2023 c. 57 art. 4 § 4. Per prior research, the 2026 session touched only § 80E.13 in ch. 80E. No audit-specific penalty; general remedies are in §§ 80E.16-80E.17.

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: Before any chargeback, reimbursement or credit arising from an audit, the franchisor must send written notice with a copy of its audit and the detailed reason for each intended item.
written_reasons_before_chargeback.quote: Prior to requiring any charge-back ... arising out of an audit, the franchisor shall submit written notice to the franchisee along with a copy of its audit and the detailed reason for each intended charge-back

chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.detail: A complaint to the Administrative Hearing Commission (AHC) filed within 60 days after written notice of any adverse decision stays the chargeback pending AHC hearing and determination. The franchisor answers within 30 days, and the hearing is held within 60 days after the answer.
chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.quote: If a complaint is filed within the sixty days, then the ... charge-back, or other determination by a franchisor which is adverse to a franchisee shall be stayed pending a hearing and determination of the matter

documentation_limits.detail: No documentation demands on warranty, sales or incentive claims more than 12 months after payment.
documentation_limits.quote: A franchisor shall not require documentation for warranty, sales, or incentive claims more than twelve months after the claim was paid.

fraud_exception.detail: With good cause to believe fraud, the franchisor may audit suspected fraudulent warranty, sales or incentive claims, and charge back fraudulent ones, for 2 years after payment (12 months otherwise).
fraud_exception.quote: if the franchisor has good cause to believe that a franchisee has submitted fraudulent claims, then the franchisor may only audit suspected fraudulent ... claims ... for a period of two years following payment

rate_submission_audit.limits: The statute sets no audit or validation procedure for rate requests. The franchisor may not require an unduly burdensome or time-consuming method or information to establish the retail rate, such as part-by-part or transaction-by-transaction calculations. A dealer may request a new labor or parts rate at most twice per calendar year. Denial of a rate-increase request can be taken to the AHC within 60 days, which stays the denial.
rate_submission_audit.quote: A franchisor shall not require a franchisee to establish the retail rate customarily charged by the franchisee for parts, service, or labor by an unduly burdensome or time-consuming method

penalties_for_audit_violations.detail: If the AHC finds a violation of § 407.828, the chargeback (or denial or reduction) is void and the franchisor must fairly compensate the franchisee within 15 days of the order.
penalties_for_audit_violations.quote: the denial or reduction of reimbursement, denial of a request for an increase in labor or parts rate, or charge-back shall be void and the franchisor shall, within fifteen days of the commission's order, fairly compensate the franchisee

states.notes: Warranty, sales and incentive claims follow the same rules in § 407.828.11. Chargebacks are limited to unsubstantiated claims audited within 12 months after payment (2 years for suspected fraud with good cause). The statute is silent on advance notice, selection basis, audit frequency, internal appeals, extrapolation and dealer rebuttal periods. The .10 cure right applies to claim submission, not to post-payment chargebacks: the franchisor must promptly flag an incomplete or inaccurate claim and allow at least 5 business days to fix it. dealer_response_period.detail: None for chargebacks. Incentive claims only: amended or supplemental claims may be filed within 60 days of when the claim was or could have been submitted (§ 63-17-117(3)).

clerical_error_protection.detail: No denial based solely on an incidental failure to meet a specific claim-processing requirement, such as a clerical error or administrative technicality that does not question the legitimacy of a claim.
clerical_error_protection.quote: deny a claim based solely on a motor vehicle dealer's incidental failure to comply with a specific claim processing requirement … such as a clerical error or other administrative technicality

documentation_limits.quote: that the motor vehicle dealer failed to reasonably substantiate the repair in accordance with the manufacturer's or distributor's reasonable written claim requirement

more_quotes.quote: No claim which has been approved and paid may be charged back to the motor vehicle dealer unless it can be shown by a preponderance of the evidence

fraud_exception.detail: The warranty and incentive audit and chargeback limits do not apply to intentionally false or fraudulent claims. No outer limit is stated.
fraud_exception.quote: Limitations on warranty parts, service compensation, sales incentive audits, rebates or other forms of incentive compensation, chargebacks for warranty parts or service compensation … shall not be effective in the case of intentionally false or fraudulent claims.

rate_submission_audit.limits: The submitted markup or rate is presumed reasonable and takes effect 45 days after receipt unless rebutted in that period. Only one rebuttal is allowed, with no later additions. If the calculated rate is substantially higher or lower than the rate on record, the mfr may request additional ROs for the 60 days before or after the submitted period, and has 45 days from receipt to rebut. rate_submission_audit.quote: the manufacturer may, in accordance with this subsection, request additional repair orders for a period of either sixty (60) days prior to or sixty (60) days subsequent to the time period for which the repair orders were submitted

more_quotes.quote: the manufacturer may not submit more than one (1) such rebuttal to the dealer, and may not thereafter add to, expand, supplement, or otherwise modify any element thereof

Incentive audit window: within 12 months after payment of the disputed claim or the end of the program, whichever is later (§ 63-17-117(1)). Chargeback grounds (2): false or fraudulent, improper or unnecessary repairs under accepted workmanship standards, or failure to substantiate under a reasonable written claim requirement, all proven by a preponderance. audit_frequency_limit.quote: A franchisor may reasonably and periodically audit a motor vehicle dealer to determine the validity of paid claims or charge-backs for customer or dealer incentives.

clerical_error_protection.quote: A manufacturer may not deny a claim based solely on a dealer's incidental failure to comply with a specific claim processing requirement, such as a clerical error or other administrative technicality

fraud_exception.quote: Subsection (10) does not prohibit a franchisor from making charge-backs to a dealer for fraud at any time as permitted by 27-2-203.

rate_submission_audit.limits: Objection only. The franchisor gets one written objection, received within 30 days, stating that the declared rate or markup is materially inaccurate. INCENTIVE (§ 61-4-204(7), (10)-(11)): audits must be reasonable and periodic. Disapproved claims need written grounds ((12)(b)), but the statute has no chargeback-specific written-notice, stay or internal-appeal rule. selection_basis_disclosed.quote: the manufacturer shall, at or prior to the meeting or telephone call with the dealer's representative, provide the dealer with a written statement containing the basis or methodology upon which the dealer was selected for audit or review.

audit_frequency_limit.limit: Once in any 12-month period, separately for non-cause warranty/recall audits and for non-cause incentive audits. For-cause audits are exempt.
audit_frequency_limit.quote: Any audit, other than an audit conducted for cause, for warranty or recall parts or service compensation ... may only be conducted one time within any 12-month period
audit_frequency_limit.score_level_reason: At most one non-cause warranty audit in any 12-month period.

Chargebacks for documentation-procedure violations also require a prior certified-mail written warning identifying the specific procedure (see clerical_error_protection).
written_reasons_before_chargeback.quote: a representative of the manufacturer has met in person at the dealership, or by telephone, with an officer or employee of the dealer designated by the dealer and explained in detail the basis for each of the proposed charge-backs

dealer_response_period.detail: The dealer gets a reasonable opportunity at the meeting or call to explain its position on each proposed chargeback. No day count is set.
dealer_response_period.quote: thereafter given the dealer's representative a reasonable opportunity at the meeting, or during the telephone call, to explain the dealer's position relating to each of the proposed charge-backs.

chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.detail: Either party may petition the Commissioner within 30 days after written notice of the dispute. Once a petition is filed, any warranty, recall or incentive chargeback or withholding is stayed until the Commissioner decides.
chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.quote: Upon the filing of a petition before the Commissioner under this subsection, any chargeback ... relating to warranty or recall parts or service compensation ... shall be stayed during the pendency of the determination

clerical_error_protection.detail: No short-pay or chargeback for failing to follow a claim documentation procedure unless (1) the dealer failed the same specific procedure within the previous 12 months and (2) the manufacturer sent a written warning by certified mail within the previous 12 months identifying that procedure.

fraud_exception.quote: Provided, however, these limitations shall not be effective in the case of fraudulent claims.

rate_submission_audit.limits: The declared rate is presumed accurate. The manufacturer may rebut within 30 days after submission by reasonably showing the submission is inaccurate. It must then propose an adjustment based on the correct rate reflected in the submission within 30 days after the audit, and no later than 60 days after submission. The dealer may protest to the Commissioner within 30 days, where the manufacturer bears the burden (preponderance). No unduly burdensome method or information may be required.
rate_submission_audit.quote: a manufacturer or distributor may, not later than 30 days after submission, rebut that presumption by reasonably substantiating that the submission is inaccurate.

states.notes: Warranty/recall and incentive audits share the 12-month-after-payment lookback, the once-per-12-months limit and the fraud rules in (b). Incentive chargeback grounds are in (b2). The pre-chargeback meeting, selection-basis statement and documentation-warning rules sit in (b1), which covers delivery, preparation, warranty and recall claims. Contingency-fee auditors are banned: no auditor may be paid in any part by the amount, volume or number of chargebacks, and contracted auditors must follow the section ((b4)). dealer_response_period.detail: Incentive claims only: no reduction or chargeback until the dealer has had notice and an opportunity to correct any deficiency and resubmit. No day count is set. Warranty claims rejected for a clerical error may be resubmitted 'in a timely manner' (§ 60-1438(5)).
dealer_response_period.quote: no charge back subsequent to the payment of a claim may be made until the new motor vehicle dealer has had notice and an opportunity to correct any deficiency and resubmit the claim

internal_appeal.detail: Not mandated. For both warranty and incentive chargebacks, the dealer must first have had notice and an opportunity to use all franchisor internal appeal processes and all available legal processes.
internal_appeal.quote: the manufacturer has the right to charge back ... any previously paid claim after the new motor vehicle dealer has had notice and an opportunity to participate in all franchisor internal appeal processes

chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.detail: Warranty: chargeback only after the dealer has had the chance to use all internal appeal and legal processes. Incentive: no chargeback while it is in adjudication, internal appeal, mediation or arbitration; for adjudication or legal action, only after a final order. No setoff of dealer funds based on audit findings until a final decision on any challenge or appeal.
chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.quote: If a charge back is the subject of adjudication, internal appeal, mediation, or arbitration, no charge back shall be made until, in the case of an adjudication or legal action, a final order has been issued.

clerical_error_protection.detail: Warranty and incentive: no denial based solely on an incidental failure to meet a claim-processing requirement, such as a clerical error that does not question legitimacy. A warranty claim rejected for clerical error may be corrected and resubmitted in a timely manner.
clerical_error_protection.quote: A manufacturer may not deny a claim based solely on a dealer's incidental failure to comply with a specific claim processing requirement, such as a clerical error that does not put into question the legitimacy of the claim.

documentation_limits.detail: Incentive claims only: ambiguity or inconsistency in submission guidelines is construed against the manufacturer. A chargeback requires the manufacturer to show the claim lacks required documentation or is alleged to be false, fraudulent or a misrepresentation.
documentation_limits.quote: Any ambiguity or inconsistency in submission guidelines shall be construed against the manufacturer or distributor

fraud_exception.detail: Warranty: the audit window extends to 4 years after payment with reasonable cause (a bona fide, evidence-based belief) that a claim is intentionally false or fraudulent, and the 30-day pay rule does not bar chargebacks of fraudulent paid claims. Incentive: the 12-month audit bar does not apply if the claim is fraudulent.
fraud_exception.quote: if the manufacturer has reasonable cause to believe that a claim submitted by a dealer is intentionally false or fraudulent, the manufacturer has the right to audit the claims for four years after payment.

rate_submission_audit.limits: On a parts-markup declaration, the manufacturer may audit the submitted repair orders within 30 days and approve or deny based on that audit. The markup takes effect 45 days after approval. A denial can go to the Board, where the manufacturer bears the burden. Separately, the manufacturer may request up to 100 additional repair orders to test whether the declared labor rate or markup is materially different. Those orders come from a 90-day period the manufacturer picks within the prior 12 months, but the dealer selects them. Requests are limited to one per 12 months, and the manufacturer has 30 days after receipt to rebut. It may lower later rates if the dealer's nonwarranty retail rates are below current warranty rates. No unduly burdensome methodology may be required.
rate_submission_audit.quote: may request up to one hundred additional repair orders ... to determine if such dealer's average percentage markup rate, retail labor rate, or both are materially different than the rates such dealer has declared

states.notes: Warranty audits are in § 60-1438(5): 1 year after payment, or 4 years with reasonable cause to believe intentional fraud. Incentive audits are in § 60-1437(10)-(11): 12 months after payment or after the program ends, unless the claim is fraudulent. For incentives, any claim for sums due after an audit must be presented to the dealer within 90 days after that item's audit is completed, and no setoff is allowed until a final decision. 'Notice' before chargeback is required, but the statute does not specify its form or content, or require advance audit notice, selection basis, audit frequency or extrapolation limits. § 60-1441(5), subject to § 60-1438(5) audits, bars chargebacks made solely because a dealer filed a used-vehicle recall/stop-sale claim. The official pages now show the Laws 2026, LB 972 versions (§§ 69-70, operative 10/1/2026), and those versions are the text quoted. LB 972 moves RVs to a separate Act; the operative § 60-1438 page does not display an RV subsection, so check it after 10/1/2026.

classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.

internal_appeal.detail: Not mandated. The 30-day Board protest period runs from notice of the final amount after the dealer exhausts any manufacturer procedure to contest the chargeback (arbitration excepted).
internal_appeal.quote: within 30 days of the notification of the final amount claimed by the manufacturer, distributor, branch, or division to be due after exhausting any procedure established by the manufacturer, distributor, branch, or division to contest the chargeback, other than arbitration

chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.detail: A protest to the Motor Vehicle Industry Board filed within 30 days of notice of the final amount (after internal procedures) bars the chargeback until a final Board order. If the chargeback is affirmed, the dealer owes interest at prime + 1% from the protest filing. Absent fraud, the Board may allow installments over up to 12 months.
chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.quote: Any chargeback resulting from any audit shall not be made until a final order is issued by the New Hampshire motor vehicle industry board if a protest to the proposed chargeback is filed within 30 days

clerical_error_protection.detail: No denial based solely on an incidental failure to meet a claim-processing requirement, a clerical error or another administrative technicality.
clerical_error_protection.quote: A manufacturer or distributor shall not deny a claim solely based on a dealer's incidental failure to comply with a specific claim processing requirement, or a clerical error, or other administrative technicality.

documentation_limits.detail: A chargeback for lack of substantiation must rest on the manufacturer's written requirements in effect when the claim arose.
documentation_limits.quote: the dealer failed to reasonably substantiate that the claim was in accordance with the written requirements of the manufacturer or distributor in effect at the time the claim arose.

fraud_exception.detail: Fraudulent warranty claims may be charged back within the franchise agreement's limitation period, but never beyond the RSA 508:4, I period, counted from the date paid. No installment relief if the Board finds fraud.
fraud_exception.quote: shall retain the right to charge back a fraudulent warranty claim, subject to any limitation period established in the franchise agreement but in no event longer than the limitation period provided in RSA 508:4, I.

rate_submission_audit.limits: Declaration: the rate takes effect 30 days after submission, subject to the manufacturer's audit of the submitted repair orders. To rebut, the manufacturer must notify the dealer within 30 days and propose an adjusted markup within 60 days. The dealer may protest to the Board within 90 days, and the manufacturer bears the burden (reasonableness against same line-make dealers of similar size nearby). Ongoing: the manufacturer may audit effective rates no more than once per calendar year per dealer, using the same repair-order method and exclusions, and may reduce rates prospectively. The dealer may protest within 90 days, and a reduced rate does not take effect until a final Board order. A rate adjusted after an audit is frozen for 6 months. No unduly burdensome methods may be required.
rate_submission_audit.quote: may perform annual audits to verify that a dealer's effective rates have not decreased and if they have may reduce the warranty reimbursement rate prospectively. Such audits shall not be performed more than once per calendar year

states.notes: Warranty audits: 9 months after payment ((d)(2)). Incentive and reimbursement programs: 9 months after payment or after the end of a program of 1 year or less, whichever is later ((d)(3)). Both allow chargebacks only for false or unsubstantiated claims. The dealer may be present or represented by counsel or a designee at any audit ((d)(4)). Audits must be completed within 30 days after a franchise termination ((d)(7)). Rejection notices on submitted claims must state specific grounds ((d)(1)), but there is no chargeback-specific written-reasons rule. The protest/stay rule in (d)(5) covers any audit chargeback, warranty or incentive. The rate-audit procedure in II(b)(1)(B) is written for parts markup; labor has a parity floor and a once-per-calendar-year declaration limit. The once-per-calendar-year frequency limit applies to rate audits, not claim audits. Scope includes maintenance plans, extended warranty, CPO and service contracts issued by the manufacturer or its common entity. Source note shows the last amendment in 2013, with no 2025-2026 change.

classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.

selection_basis_disclosed.detail: For every warranty-type or incentive chargeback, the written notice due within 30 days from the audit must explain the methodology used to select the franchisee for audit or review.
selection_basis_disclosed.quote: providing written notice to the motor vehicle franchisee within 30 days from the audit, which explains in detail the basis for each of the proposed chargebacks and the methodology by which the franchisee was selected for audit or review.

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: Written notice within 30 days from the audit explaining in detail the basis for each proposed chargeback. Final notice of the final amount follows internal dispute resolution.
written_reasons_before_chargeback.quote: providing written notice to the motor vehicle franchisee within 30 days from the audit, which explains in detail the basis for each of the proposed chargebacks and the methodology by which the franchisee was selected for audit or review.

internal_appeal.detail: Not mandated. Final notice of the chargeback amount issues after the franchisor's internal dispute resolution processes are resolved.
internal_appeal.quote: After all internal dispute resolution processes provided through the motor vehicle franchisor have been resolved, the motor vehicle franchisor shall provide final notice to the motor vehicle franchisee of the final amount of the proposed chargeback.

chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.detail: An administrative or judicial Franchise Practices Act action filed within 30 days of receiving final notice stays the full proposed chargeback, without bond, until final judgment.
chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.quote: challenging the chargeback within 30 days of the receipt of the final notice, the total proposed chargeback amounts shall be stayed, without bond, until the final judgment has been rendered in the action.

clerical_error_protection.detail: No denial or chargeback because of an administrative or scrivener's error in the claim submission, for warranty-type or incentive claims.
clerical_error_protection.quote: A motor vehicle franchisor shall not deny or charge back a claim due to an administrative or scrivener's error in the submission of the claim

documentation_limits.detail: Substantiation chargebacks are limited to reasonable written requirements that the dealer was told about before the claim arose and that were then in effect ((f) warranty, (i) incentive). Under (p), the franchisor must prove that the dealer made no good-faith effort to follow reasonable written procedures, did not perform the work, or submitted a materially false or fraudulent claim.
documentation_limits.quote: provided that the motor vehicle franchisee had been notified of the requirements prior to the time the claim arose and the requirements were in effect at the time the claim arose.

fraud_exception.detail: Warranty, extended-warranty and service-plan claims: no 12-month audit limit if the franchisor has reasonable grounds to believe the claim was fraudulent. The 12-month limit for incentive claims in (i) states no fraud exception.
fraud_exception.quote: A motor vehicle franchisor shall not audit a claim after the expiration of 12 months following the payment of the claim unless the motor vehicle franchisor has reasonable grounds to believe that the claim was fraudulent

rate_submission_audit.limits: The franchisor may audit only the sample the dealer submitted. Any proposed adjustment to the labor rate, parts markup or retail labor-time allowance must rest only on an audit of that sample. The rate takes effect 30 days after declaration, and the statute sets no deadline for the audit or adjustment. A dealer may request changes at most twice per calendar year.
rate_submission_audit.quote: The average retail labor rate so declared shall go into effect 30 days following the declaration subject to audit by the motor vehicle franchisor only of the sample submitted by the motor vehicle franchisee.

states.notes: Text is P.L.2025, c.140, § 7, approved 9/11/2025. Per § 8 it takes effect on the first day of the seventh month after enactment (4/1/2026), applies to franchise agreements in effect on or after that date, and is not retroactive to earlier causes of action. It was read from the enrolled law on pub.njleg.gov; the codified text on the NJ statutes site was not checked. Warranty-type claims ((f)) cover warranty, extended warranty, maintenance and service-related plans: 12-month audit window after payment (fraud excepted), and chargeback only if false or fraudulent, labor not properly performed, work unnecessary, or not reasonably substantiated. Incentive, bonus, sales and performance claims ((i)): 12-month audit window, with no fraud exception stated. The (p) rules apply to both: written notice with the selection methodology within 30 days, final notice, stay without bond, franchisor's burden of proof, and no chargeback for scrivener's error. Disapprovals need written grounds ((f), (i)). The statute is silent on advance notice, audit frequency and extrapolation.

classification.rate_validation_basis: Limited: the manufacturer may check the rate only against the dealer's own submitted ROs (or has no rebuttal right at all), with no right to request additional ROs or run periodic re-verification, and no comparison with other dealers' rates.

dealer_response_period.detail: A paid claim or incentive may not be charged back for an incidental claim-requirement failure, clerical error or technicality if the dealer corrects it under licensee guidelines within 90 days of learning of it and documents the need for the repair.
dealer_response_period.quote: as long as the dealer corrects the clerical error or other technicality according to licensee guidelines within ninety days of learning of the clerical error or other technicality

clerical_error_protection.detail: Covers paid warranty, recall and customer or dealer incentive claims. Protection depends on correction within 90 days and documentation of the need for the repair. It binds successor manufacturers and distributors.
clerical_error_protection.quote: shall not charge back an element of a paid claim, customer or dealer incentive, recall claim or warranty claim based on a dealer's incidental failure to comply with a claim requirement or a clerical error or other technicality

documentation_limits.detail: For warranty or recall repairs found during a separate customer repair, the documentation required to show the need for the repair may not be unreasonably burdensome.
documentation_limits.quote: provided that the dealer provides the required documentation, which shall not be unreasonably burdensome, demonstrating the need for the repair.

fraud_exception.detail: Warranty and recall: fraudulent claims may be audited and charged back for as long as a fraud action could be brought under state law. Sales and service incentives: the 6-month limit does not apply when there is reasonable suspicion of fraud.
fraud_exception.quote: the manufacturer may audit and charge the dealer for any fraudulent claims during any period for which an action for fraud may be commenced under applicable state law.

rate_submission_audit.limits: No express audit procedure or response deadline. The manufacturer need not honor a proposed increase if it can show the rate was calculated incorrectly or unreasonably exceeds all other dealers of the same or a competing line in the relevant market area; the dealer may then resubmit. The manufacturer may not require another methodology for parts markup, or unduly burdensome information such as part-by-part or transaction-by-transaction calculations. A markup change takes effect 30 days after submission, and increases are limited to twice per calendar year.
rate_submission_audit.quote: If a manufacturer can demonstrate that the rates under Subsection C or D of this section were incorrectly calculated by a dealer or unreasonably exceed those of all other franchised motor vehicle dealers in the same relevant market area

states.notes: Warranty and recall audits: 6 months after payment, for unsubstantiated, incorrect or false claims (§ 57-16-7(G)). Sales and service incentive audits: 6 months after payment or credit (§ 57-16-7.1). Disapproved claims need written reasons (§ 57-16-7(H)), but nothing is specific to chargebacks. The statute is silent on advance notice, selection basis, audit frequency, internal appeal, stays and extrapolation. § 57-16-5(EE), subject to § 57-16-7 audit rights, bars chargebacks or incentive cuts made solely because a dealer submitted a stop-sale or do-not-drive recall claim.
