classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.

dealer_response_period.detail: The manufacturer must accept an amended claim submitted within 60 days after it notifies the dealer of a disapproval based on a claim-processing failure, such as a clerical error or administrative technicality. The statute ties this to disapprovals and does not say whether it reaches post-audit chargebacks.
dealer_response_period.quote: Accept an amended claim for labor and parts if the amended claim is submitted not later than 60 days after the date on which the manufacturer or distributor notifies the dealer that the claim has been disapproved

internal_appeal.detail: The manufacturer may not prohibit or prevent a dealer from appealing the results of a warranty, sales-incentive, rebate or § 482.363574 used-vehicle recall audit. It also may not require the appeal to be held anywhere other than the dealer's place of business.
internal_appeal.quote: Prohibit or prevent a dealer from appealing the results of an audit ... or to require that such an appeal be conducted at a location other than the dealer's place of business.

clerical_error_protection.detail: Failing to follow the manufacturer's claim-processing requirements is not grounds to deny or reduce a claim if reasonable documentation or other evidence substantiates it. Amended claims after clerical or technical disapprovals must be accepted within 60 days.
clerical_error_protection.quote: A dealer's failure to comply with the specific requirements of the manufacturer or distributor for processing the claim does not constitute grounds for the denial of the claim or the reduction of the amount of compensation

documentation_limits.detail: A warranty, sales-incentive or recall-compensation claim may be denied only for good cause: nonwarranty repairs, lack of material documentation, fraud or misrepresentation. Reasonable documentation or other evidence is enough despite processing lapses. A claim for a condition found during a separate repair may not be denied or reduced.
documentation_limits.quote: must not be denied except for good cause, including, without limitation, performance of nonwarranty repairs, lack of material documentation, fraud or misrepresentation.

states.notes: One rule set covers warranty, sales incentive, rebate and § 482.363574 used-vehicle recall compensation claims. Audits are barred more than 9 months after the claim was MADE (not paid) and may be conducted only 'on a reasonable basis' ((7)). The 9-month limit has no fraud exception, although fraud is good cause to deny. Disapproved claims need written grounds ((4)(b)), but the statute has no chargeback-specific notice, stay, selection-basis, frequency or extrapolation rule. Missing time limits is not a violation if caused by reasons beyond the manufacturer's control. There is no labor-rate or markup submission procedure, only the retail-parity floor in (3). The official NRS HTML drops apostrophes. History note shows the last amendment in 2017, with no 2025-2026 change.

classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.

selection_basis_disclosed.detail: Applies only if the dealer was selected because its claims looked excessive against average, mean or aggregate data or other franchisees' claims. The franchisor must then give a written statement of the selection basis or methodology at or before the pre-chargeback meeting or call.
selection_basis_disclosed.quote: the franchisor shall, at or prior to the meeting or telephone call with the dealer's representative, provide the dealer with a written statement containing the basis or methodology upon which the dealer was selected for audit or review.

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: Not a written-notice rule. Before any post-payment warranty or incentive chargeback, a franchisor representative must meet the dealer's designee in person at the dealership or by phone and explain in detail the basis for each proposed chargeback. Notice of the final amount follows internal dispute resolution (§ 465(7)).
written_reasons_before_chargeback.quote: a representative of the franchisor has met in person at the dealership, or by telephone, with an officer or employee of the dealer designated by the dealer and explained in detail the basis for each of the proposed charge backs

dealer_response_period.detail: Not counted as a response period: the only window in the statute is to protest to a board, sue, or (LA) correct incentive/sales data. At the meeting or call, the dealer gets a reasonable opportunity to explain its position on each proposed chargeback (§ 465(4)). After notice of the final amount, the franchisor may not impose the chargeback or debit the account during the 30 days the dealer has to sue (§ 465(7)).
dealer_response_period.quote: The franchisor shall not impose the chargeback, debit the dealer's account, or otherwise seek to obtain all or any part of the chargeback funds from the dealer during the thirty-day period

internal_appeal.detail: Not mandated. Notice of the final chargeback amount follows the franchisor's internal dispute resolution processes.
internal_appeal.quote: After all internal dispute resolution processes provided through the franchisor have been resolved, the franchisor shall give notice to the dealer of the final amount of a proposed warranty, sales, advertising or marketing incentive charge back.

chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.detail: An action under Article 17-A filed within 30 days of the final-amount notice stays the chargeback, without bond, until final judgment.
chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.quote: If the dealer institutes an action pursuant to this article within thirty days of receipt of such notice, the proposed charge back shall be stayed, without bond, during the pendency of such action

clerical_error_protection.detail: No denial based solely on an incidental processing failure, clerical error or administrative technicality that does not question legitimacy, provided the dealer corrects the claim under franchisor guidelines.
clerical_error_protection.quote: A manufacturer shall not deny a claim submitted under this section based solely on a dealer's incidental failure to comply with a specific claim processing requirement, a clerical error, or other administrative technicality

documentation_limits.detail: Failing to document one part of a multi-part warranty repair cannot by itself justify charging back the whole repair. Warranty denials and chargebacks require the franchisor to prove no good-faith effort to follow reasonable written procedures, or that the work was not performed ((5)). Incentive chargebacks require a materially false or fraudulent claim, or failure to substantiate under reasonable procedures ((6)).
documentation_limits.quote: the dealer's failure to document properly one part of a warranty repair that contains more than one part shall not be the sole basis to charge back the entire repair.

fraud_exception.detail: Five years after payment for fraud (one year otherwise). Applies to warranty and to sales, advertising and marketing incentive payments.
fraud_exception.quote: more than one year, or five years in the case of fraud, after the date the franchisor made such payment to the dealer

rate_submission_audit.limits: Rebuttal, not audit. The declared rate takes effect in 30 days and is presumed reasonable. The franchisor may rebut by showing it is unreasonable compared with all other same line-make dealers in the vicinity. A rejection or rebuttal for a submission error must state the reason and identify the errors specifically; the dealer then has 60 days to resubmit and the franchisor 60 days to respond. The franchisor bears the burden of proof, and no unduly burdensome method (for example transaction-by-transaction) may be required. The statute does not provide for requesting additional repair orders. The dealer may change its rate once per calendar year.
rate_submission_audit.quote: If the franchisor rejects the declaration or attempts to rebut the declaration because of an error in the dealer's submission, the franchisor shall identify with specificity the reason for rejection and identify the error or errors within the submission.

states.notes: SOURCE CAVEAT: nysenate.gov returns a Cloudflare challenge to scripted requests, and the Open Legislation API requires a key. Text was read from newyork.public.law, which reproduces nysenate.gov (last modified 9/6/2024, verified 9/26/2026 per that page). § 465(3) is oddly drafted: it bars audits or chargebacks more than 1 year (5 for fraud) after payment 'without providing a notice ... or a mechanism' giving the dealer information on the errors or issues involved. Read here as a 1-year/5-year window plus a duty to share that information; no advance-notice timing is stated. The meeting, selection-basis, final-notice, 30-day no-debit and stay procedures apply to both warranty and sales/advertising/marketing incentive chargebacks. Chargeback grounds differ: (5) for warranty, (6) for incentives. Disapprovals of submitted claims need written specific grounds (§ 465(2)). The statute is silent on audit frequency and extrapolation.

classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.

internal_appeal.detail: Not mandated. No refusal, reduction or chargeback until the dealer has had notice and an opportunity to use all franchisor internal appeal processes and all available legal processes.
internal_appeal.quote: no charge back subsequent to the payment of a claim may be made until the new motor vehicle dealer has had notice and an opportunity to participate in all franchisor internal appeal processes as well as all available legal processes.

chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.detail: No chargeback while it is the subject of adjudication, internal appeal, mediation or arbitration. For adjudication or legal action, the chargeback waits for a final appealable order.
chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.quote: If a charge back is the subject of adjudication, internal appeal, mediation, or arbitration, no charge back shall be made until, in the case of an adjudication or legal action, a final appealable order has been issued.

clerical_error_protection.detail: No denial based solely on an incidental failure to meet a claim-processing requirement, such as a clerical error, that does not question legitimacy.
clerical_error_protection.quote: A franchisor may not deny a claim based solely on a new motor vehicle dealer's incidental failure to comply with a specific claim processing requirement, such as a clerical error

documentation_limits.detail: A reduction or chargeback requires the manufacturer to show the claim lacks material documentation or is false, fraudulent or a misrepresentation (or, for export cases, (A)(20)(b)). Ambiguity or inconsistency in submission guidelines is construed against the drafter.
documentation_limits.quote: The manufacturer shows that the claim lacks material documentation or is false, fraudulent, or a misrepresentation. ... Any ambiguity or inconsistency in submission guidelines shall be construed against the drafter.

fraud_exception.detail: The 12-month limits do not apply to fraudulent claims, and previously paid fraudulent claims may be charged back.
fraud_exception.quote: provided that these limitations shall not be effective in the case of a fraudulent claim. Division (A)(18) of this section does not preclude a charge back for any fraudulent claim that was previously paid.

rate_submission_audit.limits: The franchisor may contest within 30 days of the dealer's notice. It must give a full explanation of why the rate or markup is materially inaccurate, supporting evidence and a proposed adjustment, and cannot modify the notice or grounds afterward. If a submitted set shows a rate substantially higher or lower than the one on record, the franchisor may request more documentation covering 60 days before or after the submitted period. Disputes go through the franchisor's internal dispute resolution process, with appeal to court, and the result applies retroactively to 30 days after submission. No unilateral calculation, no unduly burdensome methods, and no use of the dealer's financial statement. The dealer may set or change its rate once per calendar year.
rate_submission_audit.quote: the franchisor may request additional documentation for a period of either sixty days prior to or sixty days subsequent to the time period for which the repair orders were submitted for purposes of an alteration.

penalties_for_audit_violations.detail: Any unreasonable denial, delay or restriction of a valid reimbursement claim makes the manufacturer liable for statutory interest (R.C. 1343.03(A)) until paid.
penalties_for_audit_violations.quote: Any unreasonable denial, delay, or restriction of a valid reimbursement claim shall subject the manufacturer to interest in accordance with division (A) of section 1343.03 of the Revised Code until paid.

states.notes: Warranty, recall and all incentive claims share § 4517.59(A)(18) and (A)(20). The 12-month limit runs from the dealer's SUBMISSION, not payment, and also bars a chargeback without an audit after 12 months. Submitted claims act as an immediate automatic credit against future billings. Disapprovals need immediate written notice with specific grounds ((A)(10), 45-day decision period), but the statute has no chargeback-specific written-notice rule. It is silent on advance notice, selection basis, frequency and extrapolation. RV franchisors and franchisees are exempt from § 4517.59(A)(16)-(27) under (D), so (A)(18)-(20) do not apply to them. § 4517.59 has been effective since 9/14/2016 (S.B. 242). § 4517.52 was amended by H.B. 96, effective 9/30/2025 (rate procedure; rental reimbursement).

classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.
classification.audit_consequence_basis: Any unreasonable denial, delay or restriction of a valid reimbursement claim makes the manufacturer liable for statutory interest (R.C. 1343.03(A)) until paid.

audit_frequency_limit.quote: A factory may reasonably and periodically audit a new motor vehicle dealer or new powersports vehicle dealer to determine the validity of paid claims for dealer compensation
audit_frequency_limit.detail: Qualitative only (e.g., "reasonable" or "periodic" audits); no numeric cap. Audits must be reasonable and periodic (warranty and incentive), with no numeric cap.

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: Written notice of any proposed audit chargeback, with the specific audit results and the proposed amount.
written_reasons_before_chargeback.quote: The factory shall provide written notice to a dealer of a proposed charge-back that is the result of an audit along with the specific audit results and proposed charge-back amount.

dealer_response_period.detail: Not counted as a response period: the only window in the statute is to protest to a board, sue, or (LA) correct incentive/sales data. The dealer may protest to the Oklahoma New Motor Vehicle Commission within 30 days after receiving the chargeback notice or the audit results, whichever is later. The factory may not implement the chargeback or debit the account until that period passes or the Commission rules, unless the dealer agrees. In titling/export cases, the factory may require supporting documentation within 30 days of notice.
dealer_response_period.quote: A dealer that receives notice of a proposed charge-back pursuant to a factory's audit has the right to file a protest with the Commission within thirty (30) days after receipt of the notice

chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.detail: No chargeback or account debit until the protest period has passed or the Commission issues a final adjudication, whichever is later, unless the dealer has agreed to the chargeback.
chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.quote: The factory is prohibited from implementing the charge-back or debiting the dealer's account until either the time frame for filing a protest has passed or a final adjudication is rendered by the Commission, whichever is later

documentation_limits.detail: Deny or charge back only if the claim was false or fraudulent, or the dealer failed to reasonably substantiate it under the factory's written reasonable procedures. No denial or chargeback because a buyer failed to title or register the vehicle, though the factory may require specified documentation (sale, delivery, qualification, export attestation) within 30 days.
documentation_limits.quote: unless the factory can show that the claim was false or fraudulent or that the new motor vehicle dealer or new powersports vehicle dealer failed to reasonably substantiate the claim by the written reasonable procedures of the factory.

fraud_exception.detail: The one-year warranty and incentive audit windows do not apply in cases of suspected fraud.
fraud_exception.quote: Except in cases of suspected fraud, audits of warranty payments shall only be for the one-year period immediately following the date of the payment.

rate_submission_audit.limits: Written rebuttal within 45 days, reasonably showing the rate is inaccurate or incomplete, with reasons, an explanation, all calculations and a proposed adjustment. If the submitted set is substantially higher than current warranty rates, the manufacturer may request in writing, within 45 days, all repair orders closed in the 30 days before or after the submitted set. All time periods are suspended until those orders arrive. It then has 30 days to propose an adjusted rate using the statutory formula on qualified repair orders the dealer submitted. The dealer may protest to the Commission within 30 days, where the factory bears the burden. The manufacturer may require repair orders to validate the reasonableness of the retail rate no more than once every 12 months. No retaliation.
rate_submission_audit.quote: may require a dealer to submit repair orders in accordance with this section in order to validate the reasonableness of a dealer's retail rate for parts or labor not more often than once every twelve (12) months.

states.notes: SOURCE CAVEAT: the codified text on OSCN is behind a Cloudflare Turnstile check and could not be read. Text was read from two enrolled 2025 acts on oklegislature.gov, HB 2158 and HB 2160, both amending 47 O.S. § 565 and effective 11/1/2025. Their audit and chargeback text is the same in substance; HB 2160 adds new powersports dealers. Paragraph lettering (A)(9)(b) is taken from the enrolled acts. Warranty and incentive audits share the 1-year-after-payment window and the suspected-fraud exception. The notice, 30-day protest and no-debit rules apply to any chargeback that results from an audit. Disapprovals of submitted claims need written grounds. The statute is silent on advance audit notice, selection basis, internal appeal, clerical errors and extrapolation.

classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.

dealer_response_period.detail: No denial or chargeback solely for a clerical or administrative processing error that does not affect legitimacy, if the dealer resubmits a compliant claim within 45 days after the initial denial or chargeback. The same rule was (5)(b) in the pre-2026 text.
dealer_response_period.quote: if the dealer resubmits the claim in compliance with the manufacturer's, distributor's or importer's claim processing procedure within 45 days after the manufacturer, distributor or importer initially denies or charges back the claim.

clerical_error_protection.detail: No denial or chargeback solely for a clerical or administrative error in following a claim-processing procedure, if the dealer resubmits within 45 days. Applies to franchises before and after 2026.
clerical_error_protection.quote: Deny or charge back a dealer's claim solely because a dealer failed to comply with a specific claim processing procedure because of a clerical or administrative error that does not affect the legitimacy of the dealer's claim

documentation_limits.detail: Franchises entered or renewed on or after 1/1/2026: the manufacturer may require only 'reasonable documentation' to substantiate a claim ((5)(a)), and may not reduce a claim payment solely on a national market norm or average ((6)(d)).
documentation_limits.quote: Reduce a payment for a dealer's claim solely on the basis of a national market norm or market average.

fraud_exception.detail: ORS 650.130(8): an audit starting more than 1 year after payment is allowed only with reasonable grounds to believe fraud, and then only amounts the manufacturer proves fraudulent may be charged back. ORS 650.158(5)(b), for post-2026 franchises, states no fraud exception to its 1-year audit window.
fraud_exception.quote: If a manufacturer ... initiates an audit more than one year following the date of payment, the manufacturer ... may charge back to the dealer only the amount of a claim that the manufacturer ... proves was fraudulent.

rate_submission_audit.limits: The manufacturer may contest with evidence that the proposal is inaccurate, or that it does not reasonably match same line-make dealers' rates in contiguous market areas or other relevant evidence. A comparison must rely on at least three dealers in the contiguous area or in an economically similar market in the region. The adjustment must be proposed within 30 days after submission, and an uncontested proposal is approved at 30 days. The manufacturer may verify the dealer's hourly rate or parts amount no more than once per year (pre-2026 text: 'Once per year') and cut compensation prospectively if it has decreased.
rate_submission_audit.quote: Not more than once per year, a manufacturer, distributor or importer may verify the dealer's hourly rate or the amount for parts the dealer charges nonwarranty customers

states.notes: CORRECTION TO EXISTING RECORD: the current audit-fields.json says pre-2026 franchises have no statutory audit or chargeback lookback. That is wrong. ORS 650.130(8) (2025 ed.), formerly (8) warranty and (9) incentives in the 2023 ed., bars INITIATING an audit of paid warranty or incentive claims, or chargebacks for them, more than one year after payment unless the manufacturer has reasonable grounds to believe fraud. After one year, only proven fraudulent amounts may be charged back. Parties must cooperate so that permitted audits conclude within 60 days after they begin. HB 2127 (2025 c.50) merged former (8) and (9) into one (8). It also added § 650.158(5)-(6): reasonable documentation, audit within 1 year after payment, chargeback only for unsubstantiated, false or fraudulent claims, and no national-norm reductions or failure-rate caps. HB 2127 § 10 applies these amendments (including to 650.130 and 650.158) to franchises entered or renewed on or after the Act's effective date (1/1/2026); older franchises keep the 2023-edition text, which has the same 1-year audit rule for both warranty and incentives. Disapprovals need written grounds (§ 650.158(4)(e)), with 30 days to correct and resubmit ((4)(c), new). The statute is silent on advance notice, selection basis, frequency, chargeback notice, internal appeal, stays and extrapolation. General remedies are in § 650.170 (injunction, damages, fees).

classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: After any internal appeal, and at least 30 days before charging back claims alleged to be false or unsubstantiated, the manufacturer must notify the dealer in writing of the amount of and basis for each claim and the total amount to be charged back.
written_reasons_before_chargeback.quote: the manufacturer or distributor shall notify the new vehicle dealer in writing of all of the following: (A) The amount of and basis for each claim the manufacturer or distributor seeks to charge back.

dealer_response_period.detail: Not counted as a response period: the only window in the statute is to protest to a board, sue, or (LA) correct incentive/sales data. Written notice must precede the chargeback by at least 30 days. During that window the dealer may file a protest with the State Board of Vehicle Manufacturers, Dealers and Salespersons (§ 306). No separate rebut-to-manufacturer period is stated.
dealer_response_period.quote: During the 30-day time period under subparagraph (i), a new vehicle dealer may file with the board a protest of the charge-backs as provided for under section 306.

internal_appeal.detail: Statute assumes a manufacturer internal appeal 'pursuant to the manufacturer's or distributor's policy manual' (the 30-day notice follows its completion) but does not require one.
internal_appeal.quote: After the completion of any internal appeal process pursuant to the manufacturer's or distributor's policy manual

chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.detail: If the dealer files a Board protest within the 30-day window, the manufacturer may not charge back until the Board holds a hearing, and may not charge back at all if the Board finds good cause to bar it. In dealer protests the manufacturer bears the burden of proving no violation (§ 306(d)(3)).
chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.quote: the manufacturer or distributor shall not charge back the new vehicle dealer: (A) until the board has held a hearing; or

documentation_limits.detail: At the claim stage, a claim may not be denied or reduced if the dealer reasonably substantiated it under the manufacturer's reasonable written requirements, notified before and in effect when the claim arose. Audit chargebacks are limited to 'false or unsubstantiated' claims ((e)(2)).
documentation_limits.quote: shall not deny a claim or reduce the amount to be reimbursed if the dealer has reasonably substantiated the claim in accordance with reasonable written requirements of the manufacturer or distributor

fraud_exception.detail: With evidence of fraud, the manufacturer may audit beyond the 9-month window and charge back fraudulent claims, subject to the 42 Pa.C.S. limitations period.
fraud_exception.quote: If there is evidence of fraud, this subsection does not limit the right of the manufacturer or distributor to audit for longer periods and charge back for any fraudulent claim

rate_submission_audit.limits: The declared labor rate or parts markup is presumed reasonable. It takes effect in 60 days unless the franchisor audits the submitted ROs and rebuts within 60 days by substantiating that the rate is 'unreasonable or materially inaccurate'. The manufacturer must propose an adjusted rate within 60 days of submission and give the dealer written support. At a Board protest it must prove both the rebuttal and the reasonableness of its adjustment. It may not require an unduly burdensome method or part-by-part or transaction-by-transaction calculations. Separately, it may run annual audits to verify that effective rates have not decreased, and if they have, reduce the rate prospectively. The dealer may declare at most once per calendar year.
rate_submission_audit.quote: A manufacturer or distributor may perform annual audits to verify that a dealer's effective rates have not decreased.

penalties_for_audit_violations.detail: A timely dealer protest bars the chargeback until the Board hearing. The Board may refuse to permit the chargeback for good cause. In a dealer protest the manufacturer bears the burden of proving no violation, and the protested action is not effective until the Board's final determination (§ 306(d)(3)-(4)). General BOVA remedies also apply: license discipline (§ 318), penalties (§ 328) and civil action (§ 329).
penalties_for_audit_violations.quote: It shall be the burden of the automobile, motorcycle or truck manufacturer to prove it has not violated any provision of this chapter as set forth in the protest filed by the new vehicle dealer.

states.notes: Warranty, recall, service-contract and incentive/reimbursement-program claims all fall under § 307(e): same 9-month audit window from payment or credit, same written-notice and Board-protest procedure, so there is no warranty/incentive split. Chargebacks are limited to 'false or unsubstantiated' claims. No advance-notice, selection-basis, audit-frequency or extrapolation rules. Recall and stop-sale claims (§ 307.1(c)) follow § 307 limits. § 307.1(b) bars cutting compensation, including by chargeback, because a recall claim was submitted. § 307 excludes RVs ((g)) and covers medium/heavy truck component and engine makers ((f)). Last amended 2018 (Act 134). Pending SB 1182 (2025-26) is not law.

classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: Current text (through 9/30/2026) mentions only 'notification' of a chargeback and does not specify its content. From 10/1/2026, for incidental-failure chargebacks, the notice must be written and identify the specific claim documentation procedure(s) violated. See changes_effective_2026_10_01.

dealer_response_period.detail: Applies only to chargebacks for an 'incidental failure' (clerical error or administrative technicality). The dealer has at least 60 days from notification to resubmit, and a properly resubmitted claim cannot then be charged back. No general rebuttal period applies to other chargebacks. The same 60 days applies to incentive claims (§ 31-5.1-21(c)(1)(ii)).
dealer_response_period.quote: A dealer shall have no less than sixty (60) days from the date of notification by a manufacturer or distributor of a charge back to the dealer to resubmit a claim for payment or compensation

clerical_error_protection.detail: No chargeback based solely on an incidental failure to meet a specific claim-processing requirement (clerical error or administrative technicality that does not question the claim's legitimacy), once the dealer properly resubmits. Identical rule for incentive claims (§ 31-5.1-21(c)(1)(i)).
clerical_error_protection.quote: shall not charge back a claim based solely on a motor vehicle dealer’s incidental failure to comply with a specific claim processing requirement, such as a clerical error or other administrative technicality

fraud_exception.detail: The 12-month limit and the clerical-error rules do not limit chargebacks for claims 'proven to be fraudulent'. No separate fraud period is stated. Same for incentive claims (§ 31-5.1-21(c)(2)).
fraud_exception.quote: This subdivision does not limit the right of a manufacturer or distributor to charge back for any claim that is proven to be fraudulent.

rate_submission_audit.limits: Declared parts markup and labor rate take effect 30 days after declaration, 'subject to audit of the submitted repair orders by the franchisor' and rebuttal. Rebuttal within 30 days of submission must 'reasonably substantiate' that the rate is unfair and unreasonable compared with all other same line-make dealers in the vicinity (from 10/1/2026 the PARTS test compares 'advertised retail rates' for warranty-like repairs in the relevant market area). An adjustment must be proposed within 30 days of submission. The dealer may protest to the Department within 30 days, and the manufacturer bears the burden. No unduly burdensome method or part-by-part/transaction-by-transaction calculations. The dealer may declare at most twice per calendar year.
rate_submission_audit.quote: The average labor rate shall go into effect thirty (30) days following the declaration, subject to audit of the submitted repair orders by the franchisor and a rebuttal of the declared rate.

changes_effective_2026_10_01.act: P.L. 2026, ch. 179 (H 8213 Sub A) and ch. 180 (S 2347 Sub A), identical text, enacted 6/22/2026, effective 10/1/2026

audit_frequency_limit.limit: No 'unreasonable' warranty audit or chargeback (qualitative standard, no numeric cap). Either party may appeal to the Department.
audit_frequency_limit.quote: A manufacturer, distributor, or factory branch shall not unreasonably subject a dealer to a warranty audit or chargeback.
audit_frequency_limit.pinpoint: R.I. Gen. Laws § 31-5.1-6(h) as amended by P.L. 2026, ch. 180, § 1

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: For incidental-failure chargebacks: written notification of the PROPOSED chargeback identifying the specific claim documentation procedure(s) violated. written_reasons_before_chargeback.quote: no less than sixty (60) days from the date of written notification by a manufacturer, distributor, or factory branch or distributor of a proposed charge back identifying the specific claim documentation procedure or procedures violated by the dealer
written_reasons_before_chargeback.pinpoint: R.I. Gen. Laws § 31-5.1-6(i)(3)(iii) as amended by P.L. 2026, ch. 180, § 1

penalties_for_audit_violations.detail: Disputes under new (h) (unreasonable audits or chargebacks; technician qualifications) may be appealed by either party to 'the department' (the agency defined in ch. 31-5.1).
penalties_for_audit_violations.quote: Either party may appeal provisions of this subsection to the department.
penalties_for_audit_violations.pinpoint: R.I. Gen. Laws § 31-5.1-6(h) as amended by P.L. 2026, ch. 180, § 1

changes_effective_2026_10_01.other: New (i)(4): written disapproval with detailed reasons within 45 days, and the dealer gets 45 days to resubmit. For time-based denials, the burden is on the manufacturer to prove the technician did not spend the submitted time. The manufacturer may protest a corrected claim to the Department within 30 days and bears the burden. Warranty labor is now paid on technician time-punch plus a dealer attestation ((c)). § 31-5.1-6(i) now also covers § 31-5.1-6.1 recall claims. 'Factory branch' is added throughout. Dealers get at least 90 days to submit claims ((a)).

states.notes: Main fields reflect the codified text in force through 9/30/2026. changes_effective_2026_10_01 shows the field values from 10/1/2026, taken from the enacted public-law text with struck language removed. Warranty chargebacks: only claims 'shown by the manufacturer or distributor to be false or unsubstantiated', within 12 months of payment or credit. documentation_limits.detail: No disapproval of a claim the dealer can substantiate under the manufacturer's REASONABLE policies and procedures. documentation_limits.quote: The manufacturer or distributor shall not disapprove a reimbursement claim if the dealer can substantiate the claim, in accordance with the manufacturer's reasonable policies and procedures.

fraud_exception.detail: Neither the 1-year audit limit nor the once-per-12-months/12-month-window limits apply to fraudulent claims.
fraud_exception.quote: The limitations of this subsection do not apply to fraudulent claims.

rate_submission_audit.limits: Within 30 days of the submission the manufacturer may request 'additional necessary documentation to support the submitted orders'. This extends its approve/deny period by 30 days. It must then approve or deny. It may not consider excluded RO types ((C)(4)(a)(i)-(vi)), and may not require an unduly burdensome methodology or information, including part-by-part or transaction-by-transaction calculations. The dealer may protest a denial in the court of common pleas within 30 days. The manufacturer then bears the burden of proving the submission was deficient, inaccurate or unreasonable, and a winning dealer's rate applies retroactively. The dealer may request a change at most once in any 12-month period.
rate_submission_audit.quote: Within thirty days of receiving the dealer's submission, the manufacturer or distributor may request additional necessary documentation to support the submitted orders.

states.notes: Warranty: audit up to 1 year after payment. Chargebacks only for 'fraudulent claims, work done unnecessarily, or work not properly performed' ((F)(1)). INCENTIVES (sales incentives, service incentives, rebates, other incentive compensation) have their own parallel once-per-12-months audit limit and 12-month window ((G)(2)). Incentive chargebacks require a showing of false or fraudulent claims or a failure to reasonably substantiate under reasonable written procedures ((H)). (I)(4) bars reducing compensation, by chargeback or incentive removal, solely because a recall/stop-sale claim was submitted. This is subject to the (G)(1) audit provisions and does not reach actions applied uniformly across the line-make. No notice, response-period, appeal, stay or extrapolation rules. General remedies: § 56-15-110 damages (not audit-specific). Last amended 2021 Act No. 31.

classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.

audit_frequency_limit.quote: A franchisor may reasonably and periodically audit a franchisee to determine the validity of paid claims or chargebacks for customer or dealer incentives.
audit_frequency_limit.detail: Qualitative only (e.g., "reasonable" or "periodic" audits); no numeric cap. Incentive audits must be 'reasonable' and 'periodic' (qualitative, no numeric cap). No frequency limit is stated for warranty audits.

The functional protection: a paid and approved warranty claim may not be charged back if (1) the repair was covered, (2) it corrected the defect, (3) the dealer documented the parts and the repair process, and (4) the dealer followed reasonable written requirements notified before the claim arose (§ 58.2). The only exceptions are false or fraudulent claims and repairs unnecessary under accepted workmanship standards (§ 58.3). At the claim stage, a claim 'rejected for technical reasons may be put into proper form' (§ 58).

documentation_limits.detail: The chargeback bar turns on documentation of the parts and repair process, and on compliance with REASONABLE written requirements that the dealer was notified of before the claim arose and that were in effect then.
documentation_limits.quote: The vehicle dealer performed the repair in accordance with reasonable written requirements of the manufacturer or component manufacturer, if the vehicle dealer was notified of the requirements before the claim arose

fraud_exception.detail: Warranty: with evidence of fraud, the audit period is 2 years from actual or constructive notice of the facts constituting the alleged fraud. Incentives: the 1-year limit does not apply if the franchisor can prove fraud (§ 32-6B-69.1). False or fraudulent claims may be charged back notwithstanding § 58.2 (§ 58.3).
fraud_exception.quote: If there is evidence of fraud by the vehicle dealer, the audit period is two years from the actual or constructive notice of facts constituting the alleged fraud.

rate_submission_audit.limits: No RO-sample submission or audit/verification procedure. In setting the warranty schedule the manufacturer must rely on the dealer's written schedule of hourly labor rates and parts. It may not require unduly burdensome documentation, including transaction-by-transaction calculations.
rate_submission_audit.quote: shall rely on the vehicle dealer's written schedule of hourly labor rates and parts and may not obligate any vehicle dealer to engage in unduly burdensome documentation thereof

states.notes: Warranty: audit any claim for 1 year after payment and charge back 'unsubstantiated' claims (§ 58). The 2023 additions (§§ 58.2-58.3, SL 2023 ch. 100, eff. 7/1/2023) limit chargebacks of paid claims. INCENTIVES (§ 32-6B-69.1): 'reasonable and periodic' audits limited to 1 year after payment, with a proven-fraud exception. §§ 58.2-58.3 apply to warranty claims only. § 32-6B-58.1 applies the same 1-year/2-year-fraud audit terms to separately warranted engines, transmissions and rear axles on commercial medium/heavy-duty vehicles at any authorized repair facility. No notice, response-period, appeal, stay or extrapolation rules. General remedies (not audit-specific): dealer civil action for injunction, actual damages and attorney fees (§ 32-6B-85); department injunction (§ 32-6B-59).

classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.

rate_submission_audit.limits: PARTS MARKUP ONLY. If the markup calculated from the submitted ROs is substantially higher or lower than the rate on record, the manufacturer may request additional documentation for the 30 days before or after the submitted period. It must approve or deny within 30 days of the submission plus any additional documentation. A denial may be appealed to the Motor Vehicle Commission, where the manufacturer must prove the denial was reasonable. It may not require an unduly burdensome methodology or part-by-part/transaction-by-transaction calculations. The dealer may request a change at most once a year. LABOR: no submission or audit process. The manufacturer may pay less than the dealer's retail labor rate only if it shows the Commission the rate is 'improper in light of all economic circumstances' ((b)).

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: No chargeback-notice requirement. Written reasons are required only when a claim is disapproved (§ 2301.404(c)) or an incentive claim is rejected (§ 2301.4749(c)). § 2301.405(a) requires the manufacturer to 'show' a permitted ground before charging back.

chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.detail: No chargeback-specific stay. A general statutory stay (§ 2301.803) bars acts affecting a party's rights once the Board gives notice of a stay in a pending complaint/protest proceeding. It is not triggered automatically by a chargeback dispute.

documentation_limits.detail: Chargebacks for failure to substantiate are allowed only under manufacturer requirements that were enforceable, i.e. reasonable (§ 2301.401(b)), when the claim was filed. The manufacturer may not require a statement of actual time spent unless actual time is the basis for reimbursement (§ 2301.406).
documentation_limits.quote: the dealer who made the claim failed to substantiate the claim as provided by the manufacturer's or distributor's requirements that were enforceable under Section 2301.401 at the time the claim was filed.

fraud_exception.detail: Warranty: no audit after the first anniversary of claim SUBMISSION unless there are reasonable grounds to suspect fraud. Incentives: no chargeback or audit after the first anniversary of PAYMENT unless there are reasonable grounds to believe fraud. After an audit, chargebacks are allowed on reasonable grounds to conclude fraud (§ 2301.475(a)-(b)).
fraud_exception.quote: may not audit a claim filed under this subchapter after the first anniversary of the date the claim is submitted unless the manufacturer or distributor has reasonable grounds to suspect that the claim was fraudulent.

rate_submission_audit.limits: The dealer's certified-mail request must include information reasonably necessary for the manufacturer to evaluate it. The manufacturer must approve or disapprove in writing within 60 days and state its reasons for any disapproval. The dealer may protest to the Board, and the manufacturer must prove by a preponderance that its disapproval or non-response was reasonable. Otherwise the Board orders the requested rate effective from day 60. The retail rate is computed as the GREATER of the 100-sequential-RO or 90-consecutive-day average from the preceding 6 months, excluding routine maintenance. Adjustments are allowed at most once a year except by agreement.
rate_submission_audit.quote: must state the requested rate and include information reasonably necessary to enable the manufacturer or distributor to adequately evaluate the request.

states.notes: Warranty (§ 2301.405): a paid claim may be charged back only if the manufacturer shows (1) false or fraudulent, (2) repair not properly performed or unnecessary, or (3) failure to substantiate under enforceable requirements. The audit window runs 1 year from claim SUBMISSION. INCENTIVES (§ 2301.475) differ: the 1-year window runs from PAYMENT, and it bars chargeback of paid amounts and of the cash value of prizes as well as audits. Incentive money may be paid only to the dealer unless it agrees otherwise. No notice, response, appeal or extrapolation rules. General (not audit-specific) sanctions: Board civil penalty up to $10,000 per violation per day (§ 2301.801), cease-and-desist (§ 2301.802), license action (§ 2301.651), DTPA remedies (§ 2301.805). Sections 2301.401-.406 are unchanged since 2003 (except .401 in 2011/2013).

classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.

audit_frequency_limit.quote: A franchisor may conduct warranty service audits and recall repair audits of the franchisor's franchisee records on a reasonable basis.
audit_frequency_limit.detail: Qualitative only (e.g., "reasonable" or "periodic" audits); no numeric cap. Warranty service and recall repair audits only 'on a reasonable basis' (qualitative, no numeric cap).

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: After an audit, the franchisor must give automated or written notice explaining the amount of and reason for each chargeback (§ 204(9)(c)(i)). Before taking control of dealer funds based on a warranty, recall repair or sales incentive audit, it must fully identify in writing the basis for the claim or chargeback and tell the dealer it has 20 days to protest (§ 201(1)(gg)(i)(A)).
written_reasons_before_chargeback.quote: Upon an audit, the franchisor shall provide the franchisee automated or written notice explaining the amount of and reason for a charge back.

dealer_response_period.detail: The dealer may respond in writing within 30 days of the chargeback notice to explain a deficiency or to provide materials that cure it (§ 204(9)(c)(ii)). Separately, it has 20 days from receiving the claim or chargeback to lodge a written protest that sends the matter to mediation and arbitration (§ 201(1)(gg)(i)(A)-(B)).
dealer_response_period.quote: A franchisee may respond in writing within 30 days after the notice under Subsection (9)(c)(i) to:

internal_appeal.detail: No internal manufacturer appeal is required. Instead, the dealer's written protest to the franchisor triggers mandatory in-state mediation within 30 days and, if unresolved, binding arbitration within 90 days of the protest (external ADR).

chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.detail: The franchisor may not take control of dealer funds based on the findings of a warranty, sales incentive or recall repair audit unless the (gg) conditions are met: written basis, 20-day protest notice, mediation within 30 days, and binding arbitration within 90 days if mediation fails. So a protested chargeback cannot be collected until the ADR process runs. The dealer cannot be required to waive this ((gg)(ii)). The conditions do not apply where the franchisor reasonably believes the amount relates to fraud.
chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.quote: take control over funds owned or under the control of a franchisee based on the findings of a warranty audit, sales incentive audit, or recall repair audit, unless the following conditions are satisfied:

extrapolation.detail: Each chargeback must rest on specific instances of material noncompliance and may not be extrapolated from a sample of warranty, recall repair or sales incentive claims.
extrapolation.quote: may not be extrapolated from a sampling of warranty claims, recall repair claims, or sales incentive claims.

clerical_error_protection.detail: A chargeback may not be based on a nonmaterial clerical error. It must rest on specific instances of MATERIAL noncompliance with the program.
clerical_error_protection.quote: may not be based on a nonmaterial error that is clerical in nature

documentation_limits.detail: During an audit the franchisor may not request documents that originated from the franchisor or its subsidiary unless the document required additional customer information (§ 204(12)). Claims may be denied for documentation only if the dealer 'lacks material documentation' (§ 204(8)(b)).
documentation_limits.quote: During an audit under this section, a franchisor may not request a document from the franchisee that originated from the franchisor or a subsidiary of the franchisor

fraud_exception.detail: The (9) time limits do not bar chargebacks for previously paid fraudulent claims. The (gg) protest/mediation/arbitration conditions do not apply where the franchisor reasonably believes the amount relates to a fraudulent act. Claim denial is allowed on a bona fide belief, based on competent evidence, of an intentionally false or fraudulent claim (§ 204(8)(d)).
fraud_exception.quote: The time limitations of this Subsection (9) do not preclude charge backs for any fraudulent claim that was previously paid.

rate_submission_audit.limits: Within 30 days of the submission the franchisor may (A) object in writing to the rate's MATERIAL ACCURACY, or (B) if the submission is substantially higher than the current warranty rate, request in writing all ROs closed in the 30 days before or after the submitted set. Clocks are suspended until those ROs arrive. Within 30 days of receiving them it may propose an adjusted rate from any set of the dealer's qualified ROs, using the same sample rules, the statutory formula and exclusions. Otherwise the rate takes effect 30 days after submission, and payment must begin within 15 days of the effective date. There is no general reasonableness challenge. The dealer may submit at most once per 12 months for each of labor and parts.
rate_submission_audit.quote: the franchisor may request, in writing, within 30 days after the franchisor's receipt of the notice described in Subsection (3)(c), all repair orders closed within the period of 30 days immediately preceding, or 30 days immediately following

penalties_for_audit_violations.detail: Audit chargebacks go to mandatory mediation, then binding arbitration, with costs shared equally. The franchisor cannot require the dealer to waive these protections (§ 201(1)(gg)(ii)).
penalties_for_audit_violations.quote: the costs of the mediator or arbitrator instituted under this Subsection (1)(gg) shall be shared equally by the franchisor and the franchisee

states.notes: Warranty parts/service, recall repair and SERVICE incentive chargebacks are enforceable only for 6 months after payment (§ 204(9)(a)). SALES compensation and SALES incentive chargebacks require written notice received within 6 months after the sooner of the dealer's sale report or the franchisor's payment (§ 204(9)(b)). The (9)(c)-(d) notice, 30-day response, clerical, material-noncompliance and no-extrapolation rules apply to chargebacks 'upon an audit' generally. (9)(d)(ii) names warranty compensation, sales incentive, recall repair and recall compensation programs. § 201(1)(gg) applies 'exclusively' to warranty, recall repair and sales incentive audits. § 204 is current version eff. 5/3/2023 (2023 S.B. 90). § 201 is current version eff. 5/7/2025 (2025 H.B. 516, ch. 280), which amended affiliate/franchise-holder provisions. The (gg) text is unchanged in the enrolled bill as read. No 2026 versions are posted for either section.

classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.

audit_frequency_limit.quote: Recall, warranty, and sales incentive audits of dealer records may be conducted by the manufacturer, factory branch, distributor, or distributor branch on a reasonable basis
audit_frequency_limit.pinpoint: Va. Code Ann. § 46.2-1571(A) (flush paragraph following A.6)
audit_frequency_limit.detail: Qualitative only (e.g., "reasonable" or "periodic" audits); no numeric cap. Recall, warranty and sales incentive audits only 'on a reasonable basis', or as 'reasonable periodic audits' (qualitative, no numeric cap).

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: The collection hold is keyed to 'final notice of the amount charged'. No statement of reasons is required for chargebacks. At the claim stage, claims must be paid or 'rejected in writing for stated reasons'.

dealer_response_period.detail: Not counted as a response period: the only window in the statute is to protest to a board, sue, or (LA) correct incentive/sales data. No collection until 40 days after final notice of the amount charged, which follows all of the manufacturer's internal processes. Within 30 days of that final notice the dealer may petition the DMV Commissioner for a hearing.
dealer_response_period.quote: Within 30 days following receipt of such final notice, the dealer may petition the Commissioner, in writing, for a hearing.

internal_appeal.detail: The 40-day hold runs from final notice 'following all internal processes' of the manufacturer. The statute does not require an internal process.

chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.detail: If the dealer petitions, the manufacturer may not collect any part of the chargeback, whether by direct payment or account debit, until the Commissioner's hearing and final decision. This covers warranty, recall, service and sales incentive, other sales compensation, surcharges, fees and penalties arising from an alleged policy violation.
chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.quote: may not collect the chargeback, fully or in part, either through direct payment or by charge to the dealer's account, until the completion of the hearing and a final decision of the Commissioner

clerical_error_protection.detail: Failure to follow the manufacturer's specific claim-processing requirements does not justify denying a claim or reducing compensation, so long as reasonable documentation or other evidence substantiates the claim.
clerical_error_protection.quote: A dealer's failure to comply with the specific requirements of the manufacturer or distributor for processing the claim shall not constitute grounds for the denial of the claim or reduction of the amount of compensation
clerical_error_protection.pinpoint: Va. Code Ann. § 46.2-1571(A) (flush paragraph following A.6)

documentation_limits.detail: Denial only for good cause, such as nonwarranty repairs, lack of MATERIAL documentation, fraud or misrepresentation. Reasonable documentation or other evidence is enough. No denial or reduction for recall/warranty repairs of conditions found during a separate customer-requested repair or made on the dealer's recommendation.
documentation_limits.quote: dealer claims for recall, warranty, or sales incentive compensation shall not be denied except for good cause, such as performance of nonwarranty repairs, lack of material documentation, fraud, or misrepresentation.
documentation_limits.pinpoint: Va. Code Ann. § 46.2-1571(A) (flush paragraph following A.6)

fraud_exception.detail: The 6-month chargeback limits do not apply where the manufacturer has 'reasonable cause', meaning a bona fide, evidence-based belief that a person of ordinary caution could hold, that a claim was intentionally false or fraudulent.
fraud_exception.quote: such limitations shall not be effective if a manufacturer, factory branch, distributor, or distributor branch has reasonable cause to believe that a claim submitted by a dealer is intentionally false or fraudulent.
fraud_exception.pinpoint: Va. Code Ann. § 46.2-1571(A) (flush paragraph following A.6)

rate_submission_audit.limits: No express audit or verification right and no response deadline. Increase requests must be in writing and based on 100 consecutive ROs or all ROs over 90 days, whichever occurs first. Only retail ROs or retail portions count, excluding menu-priced, internal, group or special-event discount, and insurance-paid work. Parts are stated as a uniform markup percentage. Disputes go to a Commissioner hearing ((F)), where the manufacturer bears the burden (§ 46.2-1573(A)). The 2025 amendments (chs. 546/558) struck the language deeming dealer-rate compensation reasonable unless the manufacturer shows otherwise.
rate_submission_audit.quote: shall be requested by the dealer in writing, shall be based on 100 consecutive repair orders or all repair orders over a 90-day period, whichever occurs first.

penalties_for_audit_violations.detail: Collection of the chargeback is barred for 40 days after final notice and, if the dealer petitions, until the Commissioner decides. In dealer-initiated hearings the manufacturer must prove good cause or reasonableness by a preponderance. Chargebacks for exported or resold vehicles require proof by a preponderance that the dealer should have known of the export or resale and failed to use due diligence.
penalties_for_audit_violations.quote: the manufacturer, factory branch, distributor, or distributor branch shall have the burden of proving by a preponderance of the evidence that the manufacturer, factory branch, distributor, or distributor branch has good cause to take the action

states.notes: Recall, warranty and SERVICE incentive chargebacks are limited to the 6 months after the DATE OF THE CLAIM. SALES compensation chargebacks have the same 6 months from the claim date. Rental-reimbursement claims may be audited and charged back for 6 months after payment of the related repair claim. One audit paragraph covers recall, warranty AND sales incentive audits, and the (F) collection hold covers all of these plus surcharges and fees, so warranty and incentive procedures are essentially the same. Claims must be paid within 30 days of submission, or 30 days after the end of an incentive program, or rejected in writing with reasons. Last amended 2025 Acts chs. 546 and 558 (eff. 7/1/2025); the official history line shows no 2026 chapter.

classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: The protest clock runs from 'notification of the final amount claimed by the manufacturer'. The statute does not specify the form or content of that notice.

dealer_response_period.detail: Not counted as a response period: the only window in the statute is to protest to a board, sue, or (LA) correct incentive/sales data. After exhausting any manufacturer procedure to contest the chargeback (other than arbitration), the dealer may protest the proposed chargeback to the Transportation Board within 30 days of notification of the final amount claimed.
dealer_response_period.quote: if a protest to the proposed chargeback is filed within 30 days of the notification of the final amount claimed by the manufacturer

internal_appeal.detail: The dealer must first exhaust 'any procedure established by the manufacturer to contest the chargeback, other than arbitration'. The statute does not require the manufacturer to offer such a procedure.
internal_appeal.quote: to be due after exhausting any procedure established by the manufacturer to contest the chargeback, other than arbitration

chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.detail: Any chargeback resulting from any audit (warranty or incentive) is stayed until the Transportation Board issues a final order, if the dealer protests within 30 days.
chargeback_stayed_pending_appeal.quote: Any chargeback resulting from any audit shall not be made until a final order is issued by the Transportation Board if a protest to the proposed chargeback is filed

documentation_limits.detail: A paid claim may be charged back for lack of substantiation only if the dealer failed to reasonably substantiate it under the manufacturer's REASONABLE written procedures OR by other reasonable means.
documentation_limits.quote: the dealer failed to reasonably substantiate the claim either in accordance with the manufacturer’s reasonable written procedures or by other reasonable means.

fraud_exception.detail: Fraudulent claims may be audited and charged back for 2 years after payment ((e)). Other warranty claims may be audited for 1 year after payment ((f)).
fraud_exception.quote: the manufacturer retains the right to audit the claims and to charge back the dealer for fraudulent claims for a period of two years following payment.

rate_submission_audit.limits: PARTS: the declared markup takes effect 30 days after declaration, 'subject to audit of the submitted repair orders by the manufacturer and adjustment ... based on that audit'. No unduly burdensome method or part-by-part/transaction-by-transaction calculations. At most two changes per calendar year. LABOR: the dealer's retail rate is presumed fair and reasonable. The manufacturer may rebut by showing it is unfair and unreasonable compared with at least four other franchised dealers in the vicinity offering the same or a similar competitive line-make. The labor rate must be routinely posted conspicuously.
rate_submission_audit.quote: subject to audit of the submitted repair orders by the manufacturer and adjustment of the average percentage markup based on that audit

penalties_for_audit_violations.detail: The chargeback is held until the Board's final order, and the manufacturer bears the burden of proof in any § 4086 proceeding at the Board.
penalties_for_audit_violations.quote: The manufacturer has the burden of proof in any proceeding filed at the Board under this section.

states.notes: Warranty: 1-year audit window after payment ((f)). Paid claims may be charged back only if false or fraudulent, not properly made or unnecessary, or not reasonably substantiated ((e)). INCENTIVE and reimbursement programs: audit and chargeback of false or unsubstantiated claims for 18 months from payment or 1 year from the end of the program, whichever is later ((g)). The (h) Board-protest stay and burden apply to chargebacks from 'any audit', so warranty and incentive chargebacks share the same procedure. Internal tension: (e) gives 2 years for fraudulent claims while (f) gives 1 year for warranty audits generally. Claim clocks are 45 days. Last amended 2021, No. 63 (eff. 6/7/2021). No later act found on the official page.

classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: No chargeback-notice requirement. Written reasons are required only when a warranty claim is disapproved (RCW 46.96.105(3)) or an incentive claim is disapproved (RCW 46.96.230(1)).

clerical_error_protection.detail: WARRANTY: no protection. Chargebacks are allowed for 'unsubstantiated, incorrect, or false' claims. INCENTIVE claims only: no denial based solely on an incidental failure resulting in a clerical error or administrative technicality (RCW 46.96.230(2)). Incentive chargebacks also require proof that the claim was intentionally false or fraudulent, or, for service incentives, that the repair was improperly performed or unnecessary (RCW 46.96.230(5)).
clerical_error_protection.quote: A manufacturer may not deny a claim based solely on a motor vehicle dealer's incidental failure to comply with a specific claim-processing requirement that results in a clerical error or other administrative technicality.

documentation_limits.detail: No limit on the documentation that can be required. The manufacturer must pay the retail labor rate for documentation work it requires to authorize or verify repairs (photos, paperwork, electronic data entry), but only once per documentation task. This is a compensation rule, not an audit limit.
documentation_limits.quote: for any documentation work required by the manufacturer to authorize or verify the work including, but not limited to, photographs, paperwork, and electronic data entry.

fraud_exception.detail: Warranty: fraudulent claims may be audited and charged back for any period in which a fraud action may be brought under state law. Incentives: the same extended audit period applies on reasonable grounds to believe fraud (RCW 46.96.230(4)(c)), and chargebacks require proof by a preponderance of intentional falsity or fraud (RCW 46.96.230(5)).
fraud_exception.quote: the manufacturer may audit and charge the dealer for any fraudulent claims during any period for which an action for fraud may be commenced under applicable state law.

rate_submission_audit.limits: PARTS: the markup takes effect 30 days after submission. The statute gives no rebuttal or audit right, bars requiring any other methodology, and bars requiring information that the DEALER believes is unduly burdensome. LABOR/DIAGNOSTIC: the manufacturer need not honor a proposed increase only if it shows the rates 'unreasonably exceed' those of ALL other same or competitive-line dealers in the relevant market area. The dealer may then resubmit. Increases are limited to once per calendar year.
rate_submission_audit.quote: A manufacturer may not require information that the dealer believes is unduly burdensome or time-consuming to provide, including, but not limited to, part-by-part or transaction-by-transaction calculations.

states.notes: WARRANTY (RCW 46.96.105(2)): audit and charge back 'unsubstantiated, incorrect, or false' claims for 9 months after payment. Fraud is excepted. Dealers must submit claims within 90 days. INCENTIVES (RCW 46.96.230) are stricter. After 1 year from payment the manufacturer may not charge back paid claims or prize value, or audit incentive compliance, absent reasonable grounds to believe fraud. Chargebacks require completing an audit and proving by a preponderance intentional falsity or fraud, or improper/unnecessary service-incentive repairs. Dealers get 1 year after a program ends to submit. No notice, response, appeal, stay or extrapolation rules for either. General remedy (not audit-specific): Department of Licensing adjudicative proceeding or civil action for actual damages (RCW 46.96.260). 2026 c 186 amended RCW 46.96.010 and .185 (direct-sale EV manufacturer provisions), not the audit rules. RCW 46.96.105 was last amended by 2014 c 214.

classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.

fraud_exception.detail: With evidence of fraud, the manufacturer may audit beyond 1 year (warranty) or 2 years (incentives) and charge back fraudulent claims, subject to the § 893.93(1)(cm) limitations period.
fraud_exception.quote: If there is evidence of fraud, this subsection does not limit the right of the manufacturer to audit for longer periods and charge back for any fraudulent claim, subject to the limitations period under s. 893.93 (1) (cm).

rate_submission_audit.limits: Within 30 days of the submission the manufacturer must BEGIN paying the rate or markup 'substantiated by the submission'. If it disputes the claimed rate, it must give written notice explaining why and stating the rate it finds substantiated by the submission. Parts: no violation if the manufacturer shows the markup is not reasonably competitive with similarly situated Wisconsin dealers ((5)). MOTORCYCLE makers may require, at reasonable intervals, documents on a reasonable number of retail parts sales to substantiate the dealer's notice ((4)). No statutory resubmission frequency limit.
rate_submission_audit.quote: A notice under this paragraph shall include a written explanation of the reason for the dispute, including the labor rate or markup that the manufacturer, importer, or distributor has determined is substantiated by the submission.

states.notes: WARRANTY (§ 218.0125(7)): audit claims for 1 year after payment and charge back amounts paid on 'false or unsubstantiated' claims. INCENTIVE and promotional allowances (§ 218.0126) use the same wording with a 2-YEAR audit window and the same fraud carve-out. No notice, selection, frequency, response, appeal, stay, clerical-error, documentation or extrapolation rules. A § 218.0125 violation is a license ground (§ 218.0116(1)(km)). Dealer damages are available under § 218.0163 (not audit-specific). History: 1999 a. 31; 2011 a. 91; 2015 a. 171; 2017 a. 235. No 2025-26 act shown.

classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.

written_reasons_before_chargeback.detail: Chargebacks require prior 'notice' and an opportunity to support the claim, but the statute does not say the notice must be written or state reasons. Written grounds are required for claim DISAPPROVALS (§ 17A-6A-8a(k)).
written_reasons_before_chargeback.quote: Charge back may not be made until the dealer has had notice and an opportunity to support the claim in question.

dealer_response_period.detail: No chargeback until the dealer has had notice and a chance to support the claim within 30 days of receiving the chargeback notice (§ 10(b)(19)). The dealer also has 30 days to respond to any audit (§ 8a(k)).
dealer_response_period.quote: A charge back may not be made until the dealer has had notice and an opportunity to support the claim in question within 30 days of receiving notice of the charge back.

clerical_error_protection.detail: A properly submitted, otherwise valid claim may not be denied for a clerical error or omission, a non-material processing requirement or administrative technicality, a different level of technician certification, or failure to subscribe to the manufacturer's computerized training. Chargeback grounds for paid claims ((k)) do not include clerical errors.
clerical_error_protection.quote: An otherwise valid reimbursement claim may not be denied once properly submitted within manufacturers' submission guidelines due to a clerical error or omission, a dealer's incidental failure to comply with a specific non-material claim processing requirement or administrative technicality

documentation_limits.detail: A chargeback for failure to substantiate is allowed only under the manufacturer's REASONABLE WRITTEN requirements in effect when the claim arose (§ 8a(k)), described in § 10(b)(19) as 'written, reasonable, and material guidelines'. No denial based on technician certification level or the dealer's failure to subscribe to computerized training programs.
documentation_limits.quote: the dealer failed to reasonably substantiate the claim in accordance with the reasonable written requirements of the manufacturer or distributor in effect at the time the claim arose.

fraud_exception.detail: The 12-month audit limit, the notice and opportunity rule, and the substantiation limits in § 10(b)(19) do not apply where a claim is fraudulent.
fraud_exception.quote: This subsection does not apply where a claim is fraudulent.

rate_submission_audit.limits: The manufacturer must approve or rebut within 30 days or the rate is deemed approved. Rebuttal grounds are that the rate is fraudulent or inaccurate, not established per the section, or unreasonable compared with all same line-make dealers in an economically similar area of the state. The rebuttal must be a written notice with specific reasons, a full explanation and copies of all calculations, and an adjustment must be proposed within 30 days of submission. The manufacturer must rely on the dealer's declaration and may not require unduly burdensome documentation or part-by-part/transaction-by-transaction calculations. It may itself demand a recalculation under (d)-(e), but not within 12 months of the last declaration, and the dealer chooses the ROs. Audits or chargebacks in retaliation for seeking the retail rate are violations ((c)). Dealer suit in circuit court within 90 days, with the manufacturer bearing the burden.
rate_submission_audit.quote: A dealer or manufacturer may demand that the average parts markup or average labor rate be calculated using the process provided under subsections (d) and (e) of this section

penalties_for_audit_violations.detail: The manufacturer must reimburse the audited dealer's documented copying, postage, administrative and personnel costs reasonably incurred during the audit, and must bill audit charges separately. Retaliatory audits or chargebacks for seeking retail-rate compensation violate § 8a(c). General article remedies: actual damages plus up to treble damages and attorney fees (§ 17A-6A-16), and injunction without bond (§ 17A-6A-17).
penalties_for_audit_violations.quote: the manufacturer or distributor is responsible for reimbursing the audited dealer for all documented copying, postage, and administrative and personnel costs reasonably incurred by the dealer during the audit.

states.notes: The 12-month audit window runs from when the dealer MADE the claim, not from payment (§ 10(b)(19)). § 10(b)(19) applies one rule set to warranty parts and service compensation, service or sales incentives, manufacturer rebates and other sales incentive compensation, so warranty and incentive audits share the same window, notice and 30-day opportunity, audit-cost reimbursement, and fraud carve-out. Paid warranty/recall claims may be charged back only if false or fraudulent, not properly made or unnecessary, or not reasonably substantiated (§ 8a(k)). Last amended by 2024 SB 173 (eff. 6/5/2024). The official bill history lists no signed 2025 or 2026 bill for §§ 8a or 10.

classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.
classification.audit_consequence_basis: The manufacturer must reimburse the audited dealer's documented copying, postage, administrative and personnel costs reasonably incurred during the audit, and must bill audit charges separately. Retaliatory audits or chargebacks for seeking retail-rate compensation violate § 8a(c). General article remedies: actual damages plus up to treble damages and attorney fees (§ 17A-6A-16), and injunction without bond (§ 17A-6A-17).

clerical_error_protection.detail: No bar on chargebacks for clerical errors. Audits may charge back 'unsubstantiated or incorrect' claims. Since 7/1/2025 there is only a claim-stage cure: a dealer whose claim was DENIED for a processing requirement, including a clerical error or administrative technicality that does not question legitimacy, may resubmit the corrected claim.
clerical_error_protection.quote: A dealer whose claim has been denied for failing to comply with a specific claim processing requirement, including a clerical error or other administrative technicality that does not question the legitimacy of the claim, may resubmit the corrected claim

fraud_exception.detail: The 1-year window does not apply where the manufacturer reasonably suspects fraud. It may then audit for 4 years and charge back fraudulent claims 'as otherwise provided by law'.
fraud_exception.quote: A manufacturer that reasonably suspects fraud may audit claims for a period of four (4) years and charge the dealer for fraudulent claims as otherwise provided by law.

rate_submission_audit.limits: Within 30 days of the submission the manufacturer may make ONE request for additional ROs covering the 30 days before or after the submitted period, if the rate is substantially higher or lower than the rate on record. The dealer has 30 days to supply them. Or the manufacturer may contest the rate by written notice within 30 days that explains why it is materially incomplete, inaccurate or unreasonable, gives supporting evidence, and proposes an adjustment. The notice and its grounds cannot be modified later. If neither is done, the rate takes effect 45 days after receipt. A contest leads to mediation (60 days), then a dealer suit within 60 days, where the manufacturer bears the burden by a preponderance. The dealer may submit at most once every 12 months unless the rate is set by mutual agreement.
rate_submission_audit.quote: may request that the dealer submit additional repair orders if the manufacturer determines from any set of repair orders submitted under paragraph (f)(i) of this section that the dealer's submitted rate is substantially higher or lower

states.notes: § 31-16-117(d) covers predelivery, WARRANTY, SALES INCENTIVE and SERVICE INCENTIVE claims in one sentence. Warranty and incentive audits share the same 1-year window after payment for 'unsubstantiated or incorrect' claims, with 4 years on reasonable suspicion of fraud. No notice, selection, frequency, response, appeal, stay, documentation or extrapolation rules. The claim-stage resubmission right and the rate-submission process ((f)-(t)) were added by 2025 SF0106 (Enrolled Act 44, eff. 7/1/2025). Since 7/1/2025, non-house-trailer/semitrailer trailer dealers and manufacturers are exempt from § 31-16-117 (§ 31-16-124(g), 2025 HB0242). The only general penalty is a misdemeanor, fine up to $750 and/or 6 months (§ 31-16-112), not audit-specific. The official title compilation shows no section history. No 2026 amendment found.

classification.rate_validation_basis: Not limited: the statute lets the manufacturer request additional ROs or information, re-verify rates periodically, or rebut by comparison with other dealers (for example 'similarly situated' or 'in the vicinity'), or it sets no validation procedure.
